lines.name: UpperTheory.FinalTheorems.everyCharacter
lines.says: The theorem asserts, with no premises, the proposition that the code calls EveryCharacter. Unfolded, it says that for every nonzero natural number N, every Dirichlet character χ of level N with complex values and every complex number s with real part greater than 1/2, if χ is not the trivial character or s is not 1, then the library value DirichletCharacter.LFunction χ s is not zero. A wrapper theorem in the module Main, named LFunction_ne_zero_of_half_lt_re, is folded into this line and asserts a proposition called DirichletLNonvanishingRightOfHalf whose body the dossier does not show.
lines.conclusion: For all N ≠ 0, all χ of level N and all complex s with Re(s) > 1/2 and (χ ≠ 1 or s ≠ 1), the value LFunction χ s is nonzero.
lines.notation: ∀ N ∈ ℕ with N ≠ 0, ∀ χ a Dirichlet character mod N with values in ℂ, ∀ s ∈ ℂ, 1/2 < Re(s) ⇒ (χ ≠ 1 ∨ s ≠ 1) ⇒ LFunction(χ, s) ≠ 0

terms.name: EveryCharacter
terms.gloss: The dossier shows it in full as the universally quantified nonvanishing statement given above.

terms.name: NeZero N
terms.gloss: This is the library side condition that the natural number N is not zero.

terms.name: DirichletCharacter ℂ N
terms.gloss: This is a library type that the dossier names without unfolding, read here as complex-valued Dirichlet characters of level N.

terms.name: DirichletCharacter.LFunction
terms.gloss: This is a library function taking a character χ and a complex number s to a complex number, and the dossier does not unfold it.

terms.name: DirichletLNonvanishingRightOfHalf
terms.gloss: This is the proposition stated by the folded wrapper theorem, and the dossier shows no body for it.

lines.suggests: The names suggest that LFunction is the analytically continued Dirichlet L-function, in which case the statement says no Dirichlet L-function has a zero with real part above 1/2, a form of the generalized Riemann hypothesis that includes the Riemann zeta function at N = 1, and the wrapper name suggests it restates the same claim.
lines.why: The statement of the head and the one definition it names are shown in full, and the names of the standard library remain unfolded. The proposition DirichletLNonvanishingRightOfHalf of the wrapper also remains unfolded in the dossier. The dossier shows nothing about the proof or the axioms it relies on.

second.says: The theorem states, with no hypotheses, the proposition that the code calls EveryCharacter. Unfolded, it says that for every natural number N that is not zero, every Dirichlet character χ of modulus N with complex values and every complex number s, if 1/2 is less than the real part of s and either χ is not the trivial character 1 or s is not 1, then the Dirichlet L-function of χ at s is not zero. A wrapper theorem in module Main, LFunction_ne_zero_of_half_lt_re, is folded into this line and asserts a proposition that the code calls DirichletLNonvanishingRightOfHalf, whose body the dossier does not show.
second.conclusion: for all nonzero N, all Dirichlet characters χ modulo N and all complex s with 1/2 < Re s and (χ ≠ 1 or s ≠ 1), the value LFunction χ s is not 0

lines.name: UpperTheory.FinalTheorems.everyCharacter_of_row
lines.says: The theorem says that if the proposition Row0b holds for the notion Rc that sends a pair (h, rc) to the condition IsRecT h rc, then EveryCharacter holds. The premise Row0b says that for every CM number field E with algebraic closure Ω, every prime l, every ring isomorphism ι from Qbar l to ℂ, every natural number a ≥ 1, every π of type CuspSub E a and every χ of type HChar over the maximal real subfield of E, if the class of π satisfies a condition that the code calls IsRegAlg and the pair (π, χ) satisfies PolarizedPair, then there exist a group homomorphism r from the automorphism group of Ω over E to GL_a(Qbar l), an integer wt and a function HT from the ring embeddings of E into Qbar l to multisets of integers such that PropsB Rc π ι r wt HT holds. The conclusion is the nonvanishing statement of line 1.
premises: Row0b holds with the notion Rc taken to be the map (h, rc) ↦ IsRecT h rc
lines.conclusion: EveryCharacter holds, that is, LFunction χ s ≠ 0 for all N ≠ 0, all χ of level N and all complex s with Re(s) > 1/2 and (χ ≠ 1 or s ≠ 1).
lines.notation: [∀ E CM number field, ∀ Ω algebraic closure of E, ∀ l prime, ∀ ι a ring isomorphism Qbar_l ≅ ℂ, ∀ a ≥ 1, ∀ π ∈ CuspSub(E, a), ∀ χ ∈ HChar(E⁺), IsRegAlg([π]) ⇒ PolarizedPair(π, χ) ⇒ ∃ r from Aut_E(Ω) to GL_a(Qbar_l), ∃ wt ∈ ℤ, ∃ HT, PropsB(IsRecT, π, ι, r, wt, HT)] ⇒ [∀ N ≠ 0, ∀ χ mod N, ∀ s ∈ ℂ, 1/2 < Re(s) ⇒ (χ ≠ 1 ∨ s ≠ 1) ⇒ LFunction(χ, s) ≠ 0]

terms.name: PropsB
terms.gloss: The dossier shows it as a bundle of six conditions, namely that r is continuous, that r satisfies IsSSRep, a condition away at primes w not containing l phrased with AwayB, an equality weights saying HT τ viewed in ℂ equals the multiset infChar of the class of π at ι∘τ transformed by z ↦ (a − 1)/2 − z, an equality weights_conj saying HT of τ composed with complex conjugation of E equals HT τ transformed by n ↦ wt − n, and a condition above phrased with AboveB.

terms.gloss: The dossier shows it as a nonzero complex subspace V of a space Sm E a whose elements all satisfy IsCuspForm, which satisfies IsStable and whose only stable subspaces are zero and V, where Sm, IsCuspForm and IsStable have no bodies shown.

terms.name: PolarizedPair
terms.gloss: The dossier shows it as two conditions, that χ.locInf v (−1) = (−1)^a at every infinite place v of the maximal real subfield, and a condition DualIsConjBy π (compNorm χ) whose body is not shown.

terms.name: IsRegAlg
terms.gloss: This is a condition on the class of π that the dossier names without showing any definition.

terms.name: IsPlaceOver A w

lines.suggests: The names suggest that the premise is the existence of l-adic Galois representations attached to regular algebraic polarized cuspidal automorphic representations of GL_a over CM fields, with local-global compatibility measured against a local Langlands reciprocity map, and that the conclusion is the generalized Riemann hypothesis for Dirichlet L-functions.
lines.why: The outer shape of the premise and the whole conclusion are visible, but the conditions inside PropsB, CuspSub and PolarizedPair, and LawsT, a name inside the body of IsRecT, rest on names without bodies and eight definitions were left out.

second.says: Assume the proposition Row0b holds for the recognition notion that sends a place datum h and a map rc to the condition IsRecT h rc. Then for every nonzero natural N, every complex Dirichlet character χ modulo N and every complex s with 1/2 < Re s and (χ ≠ 1 or s ≠ 1), the L-function of χ at s is not zero. Row0b says that for every CM number field E with algebraic closure Ω, every prime l, every ring isomorphism ι from Qbar l to ℂ, every natural a with 1 ≤ a, every π in CuspSub E a and every χ in HChar of the maximal real subfield of E, if (CG.mk π) satisfies a condition that the code calls IsRegAlg and PolarizedPair π χ holds, then there exist a group homomorphism r from the automorphism group of Ω over E to GL of size a over Qbar l, an integer wt and a function HT from embeddings of E into Qbar l to multisets of integers such that PropsB holds for them.
premises: h, the proposition Row0b applied to the notion fun h rc => IsRecT h rc, where IsRecT h rc means that there exist a and ha with LawsT a ha rc
second.conclusion: EveryCharacter, that is, LFunction χ s ≠ 0 for all nonzero N, all χ modulo N and all s with 1/2 < Re s and (χ ≠ 1 or s ≠ 1)
unclear: the 8 further definitions that the dossier leaves out

lines.name: UpperTheory.LiteratureTheorems.every_character_of_literature_of_vWin
lines.says: The theorem says that if the bundle OpenLiteratureStatements holds and the proposition VWin holds, then EveryCharacter holds. The bundle has three fields, of which the first and third are both the proposition Row and the second is RecTExists, which says that for every number field E, algebraic closure Ω, valuation subring A of Ω and prime w of the integers of E with a proof h of IsPlaceOver A w, there exists a map rc satisfying IsRecT h rc. VWin says that for every primitive Dirichlet character ψ the condition VWinAt ψ 401 holds, and the display below unfolds VWinAt, with the constants 401 and 1/52, the exponent 2 and an exponent 1/J for some J ≥ 1.
premises: OpenLiteratureStatements holds, that is, Row holds (listed twice under two field names) and RecTExists holds
VWin holds, that is, VWinAt ψ 401 holds for every ψ of type PChar
lines.conclusion: EveryCharacter holds, that is, LFunction χ s ≠ 0 for all N ≠ 0, all χ of level N and all complex s with Re(s) > 1/2 and (χ ≠ 1 or s ≠ 1).
lines.notation: [Row ∧ RecTExists ∧ Row] ∧ [∀ ψ ∈ PChar, ∀ eps ∈ ℝ, 0 < eps ⇒ eps < 1/52 ⇒ ∀ e from ℝ to ℕ, (∀ x ≥ 1, PageN(eps, x, e(x))) ⇒ ∃ J ≥ 1, ∃ X0, ∀ X ≥ X0, ∀ q, d ∈ ℕ, WinPair(eps, X^(1/J), q, d) ⇒ ∃ Y, X^(1/J) ≤ Y ∧ Y^2 ≤ X ∧ ∀ x, Y ≤ x ⇒ x ≤ Y^2 ⇒ VAt(ψ, eps, 401, q, d, e(x), x)] ⇒ [∀ N ≠ 0, ∀ χ mod N, ∀ s ∈ ℂ, 1/2 < Re(s) ⇒ (χ ≠ 1 ∨ s ≠ 1) ⇒ LFunction(χ, s) ≠ 0]

lines.suggests: The field names suggest that the first premise collects three results expected from the literature (a local-global compatibility result attributed to Caraiani, existence of a local Langlands reciprocity map, and Galois representations for polarized pairs) and that VWin is an analytic estimate holding on a window of scales with the constant 401, though the dossier shows that the first and third fields are literally the same proposition.

second.says: Assume a proof O of the structure OpenLiteratureStatements and a proof hV of the proposition VWin. Then for every nonzero natural N, every complex Dirichlet character χ modulo N and every complex s with 1/2 < Re s and (χ ≠ 1 or s ≠ 1), the L-function of χ at s is not zero. OpenLiteratureStatements has three fields, of which the first and the third both have the type One.M.Row (which is Row0b applied to fun h rc => IsRecT h rc) and the second has the type RecTExists, and VWin says that VWinAt ψ 401 holds for every ψ of type PChar (a nonzero modulus N with a primitive complex Dirichlet character).
premises: O, a proof of OpenLiteratureStatements, with fields caraianiLocalGlobalDual of type One.M.Row, localLanglandsExists of type RecTExists (for all E, Ω, A, w and h of type IsPlaceOver A w there exists rc with IsRecT h rc) and galoisRepOfPolarizedPairLit of type One.M.Row

hV, a proof of VWin, that is, for every ψ of type PChar the condition VWinAt ψ 401, where VWinAt ψ Ct says that for every real eps with 0 < eps and eps < 1/52 and every e from ℝ to ℕ with PageN eps x (e x) for all x ≥ 1 there is a real J with 1 ≤ J and a real X0 such that for all X ≥ X0 and all naturals q and d with WinPair eps (X^(1/J)) q d there is a real Y with X^(1/J) ≤ Y and Y^2 ≤ X such that VAt ψ eps Ct q d (e x) x holds for all x with Y ≤ x and x ≤ Y^2
second.conclusion: EveryCharacter, that is, LFunction χ s ≠ 0 for all nonzero N, all χ modulo N and all s with 1/2 < Re s and (χ ≠ 1 or s ≠ 1)

lines.name: UpperTheory.Lit.every_character_of_theta_integrals_local_matching
lines.says: The theorem says that seven premises together imply EveryCharacter. The premises are the bundle UnitaryGroupThirdPlaceHypotheses, the bundle ThetaLocalInputs, the proposition ThetaIntegralsAgree, the proposition LocalMatching, the proposition CovolumeBoundOfX, the proposition RecTExists and the proposition VWin. The conclusion is that LFunction χ s ≠ 0 for every nonzero N, every complex Dirichlet character χ of level N and every complex s with real part above 1/2 such that χ ≠ 1 or s ≠ 1.
premises: UnitaryGroupThirdPlaceHypotheses holds, a bundle of at least 28 named propositions whose listing is cut
ThetaLocalInputs holds, a bundle of at least 29 named propositions whose listing is cut
ThetaIntegralsAgree holds, a conjunction of three statements phrased with Decay, IsMatched, OneConst, Coinv, StepBeta and StepAlpha
LocalMatching holds, that is, every IsTriple datum admits some R and Rf with IsMatched
CovolumeBoundOfX holds, a statement of the form Closed FamHyp (…) with a constant C0 ≥ 0
RecTExists holds, that is, for every number field E, algebraic closure Ω, valuation subring A, prime w and h with IsPlaceOver A w there is an rc with IsRecT h rc
VWin holds, that is, VWinAt ψ 401 holds for every ψ of type PChar
lines.conclusion: EveryCharacter holds, that is, LFunction χ s ≠ 0 for all N ≠ 0, all χ of level N and all complex s with Re(s) > 1/2 and (χ ≠ 1 or s ≠ 1).
lines.notation: UnitaryGroupThirdPlaceHypotheses ∧ ThetaLocalInputs ∧ ThetaIntegralsAgree ∧ LocalMatching ∧ CovolumeBoundOfX ∧ RecTExists ∧ VWin ⇒ [∀ N ≠ 0, ∀ χ mod N, ∀ s ∈ ℂ, 1/2 < Re(s) ⇒ (χ ≠ 1 ∨ s ≠ 1) ⇒ LFunction(χ, s) ≠ 0], where LocalMatching is [∀ number fields F, E with E an F-algebra, ∀ σ an F-algebra map E → E, ∀ B ∈ Base(F, E), ∀ a, a' ∈ ℕ, ∀ G ∈ Geo(σ, a, a'), ∀ X ∈ Chars(F, E), ∀ om, om', IsTriple(B, G, X, om, om') ⇒ ∃ R, Rf, IsMatched(B, G, X, om, om', R, Rf)] and CovolumeBoundOfX is [∃ ε1 > 0, ∀ eps, 0 < eps ≤ ε1 ⇒ ∃ K ∈ TransportedAlt, ∀ Fm ∈ FamP(eps), ∀ CH ∈ ℝ, FamHyp(Fm) ⇒ Large(Fm, K, CH) ⇒ ∃ C0 ≥ 0, EventuallyAtAllPoints(Fm, p ↦ ∀ C ≥ C0, L3((p.S false), p.N C CH))]

lines.suggests: The names suggest that the first two premises collect published theorems from automorphic forms and representation theory, that the next three are statements about theta integrals, local matching and a covolume bound, that RecTExists is existence of a local Langlands reciprocity map and that VWin is an analytic window estimate, all combined to yield the generalized Riemann hypothesis for Dirichlet L-functions.

second.says: Assume seven things in this order, namely a proof P of UnitaryGroupThirdPlaceHypotheses, a proof F of ThetaLocalInputs, a proof hA of ThetaIntegralsAgree, a proof hM of LocalMatching, a proof hX of CovolumeBoundOfX, a proof hL of RecTExists and a proof hV of VWin. Then for every nonzero natural N, every complex Dirichlet character χ modulo N and every complex s with 1/2 < Re s and (χ ≠ 1 or s ≠ 1), the L-function of χ at s is not zero. The first two premises are structures of many named propositions whose field lists the dossier cuts off, so their full content is not visible.

lines.name: UpperTheory.Lit.nonempty_hyps_definite_side_of_closed_bound
lines.says: The theorem says that seven premises together imply that the type HypsAlt S0.NL DefiniteSideCondition is nonempty, which means that at least one record of that type exists. The first six premises are UnitaryGroupThirdPlaceHypotheses, ThetaLocalInputs, ThetaIntegralsAgree, LocalMatching, CovolumeBoundOfX and RecTExists (with its proof named hL). The seventh premise says that for every real number cDep the condition LinkedAt holds for the parameters parametersOfDependence hL cDep and for the rule that sends a slot Q and linkage L to SlotNormCondition Q L N, where N is the property of a family class 𝒞 given by Closed 𝒞 (Fm ↦ BoundAtTwoThreeFamilyFonAlt Fm).

ThetaLocalInputs holds, a bundle of named propositions whose listing is cut
ThetaIntegralsAgree holds
LocalMatching holds
CovolumeBoundOfX holds
RecTExists holds, with proof hL that is used in the next premise
for every real cDep, LinkedAt (parametersOfDependence hL cDep) (Q, L ↦ SlotNormCondition Q L (𝒞 ↦ Closed 𝒞 (Fm ↦ BoundAtTwoThreeFamilyFonAlt Fm))) holds
lines.conclusion: There exists at least one record of type HypsAlt S0.NL DefiniteSideCondition.

Then for every proof hL of RecTExists, every norm choice extension N over hL, every S of type SExt, every Γ of type GeoP and every condition NN on family classes, write p for parametersOfExtension N S Γ. If OpenParameterStatements p holds and LinkedAt p holds for CovolumeBoundThirdPlaceSeries, for FunctionalCondition and for the row condition sending Q and L to SlotNormCondition Q L NN, then AllRowsAlt holds for KPx, IsBuiltE p.s, IsGoodE p.s, BundleLinkage p, NN and DefiniteSideCondition.

first_errors: A says "seven of them stated as published theorems", but the Lean text puts only six of the nine premises in the namespace GlobalTheory.Published, and SiegelWeilUnitaryConvergent is named HeckeCharacterZeroLocus.SiegelWeilU.SiegelWeilUnitaryConvergent.

A says "a group homomorphism art from Ideles E to Gab E Ω", but the Lean text of GlobalArtinReciprocity writes "art : Ideles E →* Gab E Ω", which is a monoid homomorphism, and the dossier does not show that the two types are groups.

A describes CasselmanWallach as a statement about "a linear map T₀ from a Hilbert space H to a complete space E with a condition IsGKMap" and does not say that anything is left out, but the Lean text also requires "IsURepOn (UJset ε) σ", "IsIrredOn (UJset ε) σ" and "IsSmoothModRep ε p π dπ" before the conclusion.

deeper.says: The theorem assumes nine propositions taken as hypotheses. Six of them lie in the namespace GlobalTheory.Published and are named GlobalArtinReciprocity, DiscreteSeriesCover, HarishChandraModules, CuspRapidDecay, CasselmanWallach and DiscreteSeriesClassification, one is HeckeCharacterZeroLocus.SiegelWeilU.SiegelWeilUnitaryConvergent, and two are the propositions SurjectiveOntoX and LambdaLowerBound₂, each of the form Closed FamHyp. Under these hypotheses it considers any proof hL of the proposition RecTExists, any norm choice extension N over hL, any S of type SExt, any Γ of type GeoP and any property NN of family classes, and it lets p be the parameter record parametersOfExtension N S Γ, which is the four-part record made of RX, N, S and Γ. If p satisfies every part of the record OpenParameterStatements, and LinkedAt holds at p for the three row conditions CovolumeBoundThirdPlaceSeries, FunctionalCondition and the slot norm condition for NN, then the record AllRowsAlt holds. That record is built from the base predicate KPx, the slots IsBuiltE p.s and IsGoodE p.s, the linkage BundleLinkage p, the property NN and the side condition DefiniteSideCondition. In unfolded form, AllRowsAlt says that each of a long list of row conditions (class count bound, J-invariant, instance rank, divisor, primitivity, Lp, order, torsion-free and others) is linked at p in the same sense as LinkedAt. The list is cut in the dossier, so further fields that may use NN and DefiniteSideCondition are not visible.
premises: GlobalArtinReciprocity, which says that for every number field E and every algebraic closure Ω of E there is a group homomorphism art from Ideles E to Gab E Ω that satisfies IsGlobalArtin

SiegelWeilUnitaryConvergent, which says that for all number fields F and E with E an F-algebra, every F-algebra map σ from E to E with IsCMExt F E σ, every natural number M and every M×M matrix J over E with IsHermND σ J, the condition SiegelWeilAt F E σ M J holds

DiscreteSeriesCover, which says that for all natural numbers p and q with 1 ≤ p + q and every T of type GrpData p q there is a map D from the functions lam of type Ix p q → ℚ that satisfy IsParam lam to DSRep T, so that HasTypes (D lam) lam.1 holds for every such lam and every R of type DSRep T satisfies UnitEquiv R (D lam) for some lam
HarishChandraModules, which says that HarishChandraModulesOn T holds for every p, q with p+q ≥ 1 and every T of type GrpData p q, and that KFiniteAnalyticUJ holds

CuspRapidDecay, which says that for every D of type D7 and data θ, V and e meeting IsInfFam and IsExpFam, every function φ from GA D V to ℂ that satisfies IsAutFun V φ, IsSmoothInf V e φ, IsUnifModerate θ V e φ and IsCuspFun V φ satisfies IsRapidDecay θ V φ

CasselmanWallach, a long statement about a linear map T₀ with IsGKMap from a complex Hilbert space H carrying σ with IsURepOn and IsIrredOn for UJset ε to a complete Hausdorff uniform space E with seminorms p and maps π and dπ satisfying IsSmoothModRep. It asks for a complex linear map T from H to E that agrees with T₀ on all vectors satisfying IsKFin ε σ, satisfies IsSmoothGMap ε σ p π T, agrees on all w satisfying SmoothVec (lieSet ε) σ w with any complex linear map T' from H to E meeting those two conditions, has a closed image of the set of w satisfying SmoothVec (lieSet ε) σ w, and, whenever there exists v satisfying IsKFin ε σ v with T₀ v ≠ 0, gives for every list S of lists of matrices in lieSet ε a continuous seminorm q on E satisfying sobNorm σ S w ≤ q (T w) for all w satisfying SmoothVec (lieSet ε) σ w

DiscreteSeriesClassification, which says that for every natural number n there are complex inner product spaces H ε lam and maps π ε lam from n by n complex matrices to continuous linear maps of H ε lam with two properties. First, for every ε of type Fin n → Bool and every strictly decreasing lam of type Fin n → ℝ with lam a − (n − 1)/2 an integer for all a, the space H ε lam is complete and nontrivial, π ε lam satisfies IsURepOn (UJset ε), IsIrredOn (UJset ε), IsSqIntOn ε and HasInfChar ε at lam, there is a unique submodule S with IsKTypeOf ε (π ε lam) (lam + rhoN ε − rhoC ε) S, and every μ and submodule S with IsKTypeOf ε (π ε lam) μ S has μ equal to lam + rhoN ε − rhoC ε plus a sum of the terms c a b • root a b with natural numbers c a b that are nonzero only when a < b. Second, for every ε and every complete nontrivial complex inner product space H' with a map σ satisfying IsURepOn (UJset ε), IsIrredOn (UJset ε) and IsSqIntOn ε there are a permutation s of Fin n with s a < s b whenever a < b and ε (s a) = ε (s b), a strictly decreasing mu with mu a − (n − 1)/2 an integer for all a, and a linear isometric equivalence T from H' onto H (ε ∘ s) mu with T (σ (g.submatrix s.symm s.symm) v) = π (ε ∘ s) mu g (T v) for all g in UJset (ε ∘ s) and all v

SurjectiveOntoX, which says that Closed FamHyp holds for the property sending Fm and CH to the statement that, whenever DIVinN Fm holds, there are a real C0 ≥ 0 and a real x0 such that for every x > Fm.x1 with x0 ≤ x, every i of type Fm.Ix x and every point p satisfying p.PointConditions' and More p, the condition (p.S false).ON (p.N C CH) holds for every C ≥ C0

LambdaLowerBound₂, which says that Closed FamHyp holds for the property sending Fm and CH to the statement that there is a real x0 such that for every x > Fm.x1 with x0 ≤ x, every i of type Fm.Ix x and every point p satisfying p.PointConditions', the condition (p.S true).L6 (p.N C CH) holds for every C

OpenParameterStatements p, which says that LinkedAt p r holds for each of twelve row conditions r (primitivity, lambda prime, divisor, decomposition point, selection jump, the alternative tie, label, goodness, geometric weak compatibility, multiplicity, kappa and defect)
LinkedAt p CovolumeBoundThirdPlaceSeries
LinkedAt p FunctionalCondition
LinkedAt p applied to the relation that sends Q and L to SlotNormCondition Q L NN

deeper.suggests: As a suggestion only, the names hint that, given standard published results of automorphic representation theory such as Artin reciprocity, Siegel–Weil, Harish-Chandra modules and the discrete series classification, a theta-correspondence construction at a third place whose open parameter rows are linked has all of its row properties linked as well.
deeper.why: The logical shape of the statement is fully visible, but AllRowsAlt and DefiniteSideCondition are cut, and the meaning rests on many conditions with no visible body, such as Lg1, EvLg, Row, RX and most row conditions.

lines.says: Assume the proposition SiegelWeilUnitaryConvergent. Then for every family class 𝒜 and every selection σ that assigns a BundleCondition record to each family in 𝒜, each x beyond the family's threshold x1 and each index i, three statements hold together, namely SelectionLpBound 𝒜 σ, SelectionOrderBound 𝒜 σ and H_hTF 𝒜. Two wrapper theorems folded into this line state, each under the same premise SiegelWeilUnitaryConvergent, three conditions with matching names, SlotLpCondition, SlotOrderCondition and SlotTorsionFreeCondition. One wrapper states them for every slot Q and every Lk of type LkT BundleCondition, and the other states them under the operator Lg1 for every predicate KP, every pair of slots Q and Q' and every Lk of type LkT BundleCondition. The dossier does not show the bodies of these three conditions, so it does not show that they state the same triple.

terms.name: SiegelWeilUnitaryConvergent
terms.gloss: The proposition that SiegelWeilAt F E σ M J holds whenever IsCMExt F E σ and IsHermND σ J hold, for number fields F and E and an M by M matrix J over E.

terms.name: IsCMExt
terms.gloss: The condition that F is totally real, E is totally complex, E has dimension 2 over F, and every embedding τ of E into the complex numbers satisfies τ(σ x) equal to the complex conjugate of τ(x).

terms.name: IsHermND
terms.gloss: The condition that σ(J j i) = J i j for all i and j and that the determinant of J is not zero.

terms.name: SiegelWeilAt
terms.gloss: The conjunction of two conditions that the code calls FinVol and SiegelDensities, both not shown.

terms.name: FamClass
terms.gloss: The type of predicates on families Fm of type FamP eps, for every real eps.

terms.name: FamP
terms.gloss: A large record of data and conditions indexed by reals x beyond a threshold x1 and indices i, including data D x i and L x i and constants such as CTu and Csz, with the end of the text cut off.

terms.name: RawSel
terms.gloss: RawSel Bd 𝒜 is the type of rules that give an element of Bd (Fm.D x i) (objAt Fm x hx i) Fm.Csz for each family Fm with 𝒜 Fm, each x with Fm.x1 < x and each index i.

terms.name: BundleCondition
terms.gloss: A record with seven fields R, S, P, pin, DH, C and B, where DH is a pair of natural numbers (p1, p2) with D.s.Del = p1 and O.L.etaSz = D.R.m · p2, and the other fields have record types whose own parts rest on names not shown.

terms.name: SelectionLpBound
terms.gloss: LoopRowS with constant 3 on the class D3 3 𝒜 and the selection whose threshold is the first component of familySelection σ and whose data are the S fields of σ.

terms.name: LoopRowS
terms.gloss: For every real valued function aF on lists of reals, Closed 𝒞 of the property that, in the sense of OwnEv, under hypotheses called Hyp, ConcTie and AbsConv with constants Fm.CYL + 1, 1/4, 3, 1/2, Fm.CTu, C0 and aF Fm.cOut, two conditions called RowBig and RowNotScalar hold.

terms.name: SelectionOrderBound
terms.gloss: Closed (D3 3 𝒜) of the property that TheoremSSelected Fm 3 holds for the selection built from σ, for every proof hc that Fm lies in D3 3 𝒜.

terms.name: TheoremSSelected
terms.gloss: In the sense of OwnEv, under a hypothesis called hyp with constants C0, Fm.CYL + 1, 1/4, 3, 1/2 and Fm.CTu, for all distinct words u and u' the squared norm of a quantity K0 is at most (1 + 1/b⁶) · duS(u) · duS(u') / Dstar, where b is the scale entry (Fm.L x i).sc.b.

terms.name: H_hTF
terms.gloss: Closed (D3 3 𝒜) of the property TFrame Fm (Fm.CYL + 1) (1/4) 3 (1/2) Fm.CTu 3.

terms.name: TFrame
terms.gloss: In the sense of OwnEv, under a hypothesis called Hyp0 with the six given constants, for every w the product Tr(D, w) · kaS(D)^(2 · rS) is at least 1, where Tr, kaS and OwnEv are not shown.

terms.name: Closed
terms.gloss: Closed 𝒞 P says there is ε1 > 0 such that for every eps with 0 < eps ≤ ε1 there is a record K such that every family Fm of type FamP eps and every real CH with 𝒞 Fm and Fm.Large K CH satisfy P Fm CH.

terms.name: D3
terms.gloss: D3 C0 𝒜 is the family class Des (WithChN 𝒜) C0, where Des and WithChN are not shown.

terms.name: familySelection
terms.gloss: The selection that sends a family Fm in 𝒜 to the pair of the threshold Fm.x1 and the R fields of σ.

terms.name: spectralConditionOfRawSelection
terms.gloss: The rule that returns the S field of σ at each family, x and index.

deeper.says: Assume the proposition that the code calls SiegelWeilUnitaryConvergent. That proposition says the following for all number fields F and E with E an algebra over F, and every automorphism σ of E that fixes F. If F is totally real, E is totally complex, E has degree 2 over F, and every complex embedding τ of E satisfies τ(σ x) = conj(τ x), then for every natural number M and every M by M matrix J over E with σ(J_ji) = J_ij for all i and j and det J ≠ 0, the two opaque conditions FinVol and SiegelDensities both hold. Under this assumption the theorem takes any family class 𝒜 and any raw selection σ, which assigns a BundleCondition record to every family Fm in 𝒜, every real x > Fm.x1 and every index i in Fm.Ix x, and it concludes three statements. The first is SelectionLpBound 𝒜 σ, which is LoopRowS with constant 3 for the class D3 3 𝒜 and the selection made of Fm.x1 and the STies data that the S fields of σ give. It says that for every function aF from lists of reals to reals, Closed holds on D3 3 𝒜 for the statement that every proof hc of D3 3 𝒜 Fm gives OwnEv at Fm of the following. For all x with Fm.x1 < x and (sel Fm hc).1 ≤ x and all words u and u′ of (Fm.D x i).what₂.Word, the opaque conditions Cnt.Hyp, with the constants Fm.CYL + 1, 1/4, 3, 1/2, Fm.CTu, 3 and aF Fm.cOut, ConcTie and AbsConv together imply the opaque conditions RowBig and RowNotScalar. The second is SelectionOrderBound 𝒜 σ, which requires Closed on D3 3 𝒜 for the statement that for every proof hc of D3 3 𝒜 Fm, TheoremSSelected holds at Fm, 3 and the same selection. TheoremSSelected says that OwnEv holds at Fm of the implication from the hypothesis AdmissibleBoundsFromSource.hyp, taken at Fm.D x i and Fm.L x i with the constants 3, C′, Cl, Fm.CYL + 1, 1/4, 3, 1/2 and Fm.CTu, to the bound ‖K0‖² ≤ (1 + 1/b⁶)·duS(u)·duS(u′)/Dstar for every x with Fm.x1 < x and s.1 ≤ x and all distinct words u ≠ u′. The third is H_hTF 𝒜, which requires Closed on D3 3 𝒜 for TFrame at Fm with the constants Fm.CYL + 1, 1/4, 3, 1/2, Fm.CTu and 3. TFrame says that OwnEv holds at Fm of the implication from the opaque hypothesis Cnt.Hyp0, taken at Fm.D x i and Fm.L x i with C′, Cl and those constants, to the inequality 1 ≤ Tr(D,w)·kaS(D)^(2·rS) for every w, where D is Fm.D x i.

𝒜 is a family class, meaning a predicate on families Fm of type FamP eps for every real eps
σ is a raw selection that gives, for every eps, every Fm with 𝒜 Fm, every real x with Fm.x1 < x and every i in Fm.Ix x, a record of type BundleCondition (Fm.D x i) (objAt Fm x hx i) Fm.Csz

TFrame(Fm, Fm.CYL+1, 1/4, 3, 1/2, Fm.CTu, 3)), where SWUnitaryConv ≡ ∀F,E number fields, ∀σ∈Aut_F(E), [F tot. real ∧ E tot. complex ∧ [E:F]=2 ∧ ∀τ:E→ℂ, τ∘σ = conj∘τ] ⇒ ∀M, ∀J∈E^{M×M}, [σ(J_ji)=J_ij ∀i,j ∧ det J≠0] ⇒ FinVol(F,E,σ,M,J) ∧ SiegelDensities(F,E,σ,M,J), and Closed(𝒞,P) ≡ ∃ε1>0 ∀eps∈(0,ε1] ∃K∈TransportedAlt ∀Fm∈FamP(eps) ∀CH∈ℝ, 𝒞(Fm) ∧ Large(Fm,K,CH) ⇒ P(Fm,CH)

deeper.suggests: As a suggestion only, the names point to a step in a theta-correspondence argument in which a Siegel–Weil convergence assumption for unitary groups is used to derive Lp-type row bounds, order bounds and a torsion-free frame bound for families chosen through column bundles.

lines.says: Assume three global conditions that the code calls SWXS, RowNGP and RowsFinDim. Then for every class 𝒞 of parameter families and every selector sel on 𝒞, if every selected datum Fm.D x i is LocTied, and the conditions RanksRow 3 𝒞 and LoopRowS 3 𝒞 sel hold, then the off-diagonal bound TheoremSSelected Fm 3 (sel Fm hc) holds in the Closed sense on 𝒞. Unfolded, the bound says that for all large x, every index i and every pair of distinct words u ≠ u', the squared norm of the quantity K0 attached to (u, u') is at most (1 + 1/b^6) times duS(u)·duS(u')/Dstar, under a standing hypothesis with constants 3, C', Cl, Fm.CYL + 1, 1/4, 3, 1/2 and Fm.CTu.
premises: SWXS holds, which says that for every datum D and every HidaSetting X of D two conditions that the code calls SWa1 and StabilizerFirstChernCompatibility hold for the fields, the map cm.sig, rank n and matrix J of X

RowNGP holds, which says that for all reals Cg, cb, Cw, cT, CT, C0 with 0 < cb and 0 < cT there are C4 ≥ 0 and thresholds C'₀, Cl₀ such that for all C' ≥ C'₀ and Cl ≥ Cl₀ and all data satisfying Ties, Hyp0, Stand, ConcTie and AbsConv, a condition that the code calls RowNG holds with the numbers epsNG D large₂ C4 and ddC X Y u u'

RowsFinDim holds, which says that under listed hypotheses on an instance I, a Haar measure, a fundamental domain, a right regular action R, a locally constant function e supported in I.Kset, and unitary irreducible families σ with unit vectors w, the range of the composite operator Re∘T is a finite-dimensional complex vector space. This summary leaves out the hypotheses that introduce Re and T, which are I.IsRConvF μf fund R e Re and IsOpInt (muInf I) (fun g => R (g, 1)) (phInf I σ w dv) T, the condition IsFdeg on the numbers dv and the integrability of phLoc
𝒞 is any property of parameter families FamP eps and sel is any function that gives a selection SSelF Fm for each family Fm in 𝒞

for every eps, every family Fm with a proof hc of 𝒞 Fm, every x with Fm.x1 < x and (sel Fm hc).1 ≤ x and every index i in Fm.Ix x, the datum Fm.D x i is LocTied, meaning that at every nonzero prime p of the ring of integers of its field host.F there exists a LocIso between the two local objects D.s.atP p and locC D p, where D stands for Fm.D x i
RanksRow 3 𝒞 holds, which is Closed 𝒞 applied to the condition RanksF Fm 3 (Fm.CYL + 1) (1/4) 3 (1/2) Fm.CTu

LoopRowS 3 𝒞 sel holds, which says that for every function aF from lists of reals to reals, in the Closed sense on 𝒞 and eventually in x, the hypotheses Hyp with constants C', Cl, Fm.CYL + 1, 1/4, 3, 1/2, Fm.CTu, 3 and aF(Fm.cOut), together with ConcTie and AbsConv, imply both RowBig and RowNotScalar with the numbers epsL(Fm.D x i) and ddC. This summary leaves out the binders hc, hx, h0, u and u' and the object (sel Fm hc).2 x hx h0 i, and the constants C' and Cl stand for sC' Fm and sCl Fm
lines.conclusion: Closed 𝒞 holds for the property that sends Fm to the statement that for every proof hc that Fm is in 𝒞 the condition TheoremSSelected Fm 3 (sel Fm hc) holds
lines.notation: SWXS ⇒ RowNGP ⇒ RowsFinDim ⇒ ∀ 𝒞 ∀ sel ∈ SSel 𝒞, [∀ eps ∀ Fm ∈ FamP eps ∀ hc ∈ 𝒞 Fm ∀ x (Fm.x1 < x ∧ (sel Fm hc).1 ≤ x) ∀ i ∈ Fm.Ix x, LocTied(Fm.D x i)] ⇒ RanksRow 3 𝒞 ⇒ LoopRowS 3 𝒞 sel ⇒ Closed 𝒞 (Fm ↦ ∀ hc, TheoremSSelected Fm 3 (sel Fm hc)), where Closed 𝒞 P means ∃ ε1 > 0 ∀ eps (0 < eps ≤ ε1) ∃ K ∈ TransportedAlt ∀ Fm ∈ FamP eps ∀ CH ∈ ℝ, 𝒞 Fm ⇒ Fm.Large K CH ⇒ P Fm CH, and TheoremSSelected Fm 3 s means ∃ x0 ∀ x ≥ x0 ∀ i ∈ Fm.Ix x, hyp(Fm.D x i, Fm.L x i, 3, sC' Fm, sCl Fm, Fm.CYL+1, 1/4, 3, 1/2, Fm.CTu) ⇒ ∀ (Fm.x1 < x) (s.1 ≤ x) ∀ u ≠ u', ‖((s.2 x i).Y.tO u u').K0‖² ≤ (1 + ((Fm.L x i).sc.b⁶)⁻¹)·(duS u · duS u' / Dstar)

terms.name: FamClass
terms.gloss: The dossier shows this to be a property of parameter families, that is, a function that assigns a true or false statement to each FamP eps for each real eps.

terms.name: FamP
terms.gloss: The dossier shows this to be a large record, cut off in the listing, that extends a record FamCore and carries for each x > x1 and index i a datum D x i, size data L x i and many further fields and constraints.

terms.name: Closed
terms.gloss: The dossier shows Closed 𝒞 P to mean that there is ε1 > 0 such that for every eps with 0 < eps ≤ ε1 there is a record K of type TransportedAlt such that P Fm CH holds for every family Fm in 𝒞 and real CH satisfying a condition that the code calls Fm.Large K CH.

terms.name: TransportedAlt
terms.gloss: The dossier shows this to be a record of one real number pre and three functions t, mid and last from lists of reals to reals.

terms.name: SSel
terms.gloss: The dossier shows a selector to be a function that gives an element of SSelF Fm for each family Fm in 𝒞.

terms.name: SSelF
terms.gloss: The dossier shows this to be a pair of a real x0 and a function that gives, for each x with Fm.x1 < x and x0 ≤ x and each index i, an object of a type that the code calls STies (Fm.D x i).

terms.name: OwnEv
terms.gloss: The dossier shows OwnEv Fm P to mean that there is a real x0 such that P (sC' Fm) (sCl Fm) x i holds for all x ≥ x0 and all indices i in Fm.Ix x.

terms.name: TheoremSSelected
terms.gloss: The dossier shows this to be the eventual statement that the hypothesis hyp implies, for all distinct words u and u', the bound ‖K0‖² ≤ (1 + 1/b⁶)·duS(u)·duS(u')/Dstar, where K0 comes from the selected object's field Y.tO u u' and b is (Fm.L x i).sc.b.

terms.name: hyp
terms.gloss: The dossier shows hyp to be the conjunction of StandingNumericalData D C0, StandingHypotheses D large₂ C' Cl Cg cb Cu cT CT and 1 ≤ C0, where the first two are names without visible bodies.

terms.name: LocTied
terms.gloss: The dossier shows LocTied D to mean that for every nonzero prime p of the ring of integers of D.host.F there exists a LocIso from D.s.atP p to locC D p.

terms.name: LocIso
terms.gloss: The dossier shows this to be a pair of ring isomorphisms eF and eE between the local fields Fp and Ep of two local objects, both continuous with continuous inverse, compatible with the embeddings of F and E, the valuation order, the p-adic numbers, the conjugation cj, the subring O and the function psiE.

terms.name: RanksRow
terms.gloss: The dossier shows RanksRow C0 𝒞 to be Closed 𝒞 applied to RanksF Fm C0 (Fm.CYL + 1) (1/4) 3 (1/2) Fm.CTu, where RanksF is a condition that the code calls FamilyRanksHypothesis and whose body is not shown.

terms.name: LoopRowS
terms.gloss: The dossier shows this to be a statement, for every function aF and in the Closed and OwnEv senses, that Hyp, ConcTie and AbsConv imply the conjunction of two conditions that the code calls RowBig and RowNotScalar with the numbers epsL and ddC.

terms.name: RowNGP
terms.gloss: The dossier shows this to be a statement with explicit quantifiers over constants whose final conclusion is a condition that the code calls RowNG, with body not shown, taken at epsNG D large₂ C4 and ddC X Y u u'.

terms.name: epsNG
terms.gloss: The dossier shows epsNG D large₂ C4 to be the real number (2^(k − 2·rS − 5))⁻¹ · exp(C4 · (mR D)⁵ · f · log b), where k, rS, f come from D.R and b from large₂.sc.

terms.name: epsL
terms.gloss: The dossier shows epsL D to be the real number exp(−(1/3)·k·f·log k) with k and f taken from D.R.

terms.name: ddC
terms.gloss: The dossier shows ddC X Y u u' to be the real number duC X Y u · duC X Y u' / DstC X.

terms.name: RowsFinDim
terms.gloss: The dossier shows this to be a statement that the space HH I μf fund Re T, defined as the range of the composite Re∘T on the space I.L2 μf fund, is finite-dimensional over ℂ whenever T is given weakly by an integral of the action R against the function phInf and the listed hypotheses hold.

terms.name: SWXS
terms.gloss: The dossier shows this to be the statement that for every D and every HidaSetting X of D the two conditions SWa1 and StabilizerFirstChernCompatibility, whose bodies are not shown, hold for the data of X.

terms.name: ConcTie
terms.gloss: The dossier shows this to be a conjunction of several named conditions on X and Y, among them duC X Y u = duS u for all u, DstC X = Dstar, integrability of X.ph, and LocTied D, with most components not shown in body.

terms.name: Stand
terms.gloss: The dossier shows Stand D u u' to say that 1 ≤ rS, that Tu D u and Tu D u' are primes at least 3 that split completely in host.E, that g 0 and g 1 are distinct primes that split completely, that gS D is coprime to Tu D u · Tu D u', and that Tu D u ≡ Tu D u' modulo gS D.

terms.name: D7
terms.gloss: The dossier shows this to be a large record, cut off in the listing, that bundles ranks R, a host with fields F and E, hermitian spaces, row data what₂ with a finite type of words, a number field LL and many compatibility conditions.

lines.suggests: The names suggest a bound on the off-diagonal entries of a kernel or Gram matrix indexed by words, derived from a Siegel–Weil type input (SWXS), a row non-degeneracy input and a finite-dimensionality statement for a space of automorphic forms, but the dossier does not show this.
lines.why: The logical shape, the constants and the final inequality are fully visible, but RowNG, RowBig, RowNotScalar, FamilyRanksHypothesis, Fm.Large, STies, StandingHypotheses and the object K0 are names without visible bodies and the records FamP and D7 are cut.

second.says: Assume the three conditions that the code calls SWXS, RowNGP and RowsFinDim, and take any family class 𝒞 and any selection sel of type SSel 𝒞. Assume further that LocTied holds for the datum Fm.D x i in every selected family member, that RanksRow 3 𝒞 holds and that LoopRowS 3 𝒞 sel holds. Then there is a real ε1 > 0 such that for every eps with 0 < eps ≤ ε1 there is a K of type TransportedAlt such that for every family Fm of type FamP eps and every real CH with 𝒞 Fm and Fm.Large K CH, every proof hc of 𝒞 Fm gives TheoremSSelected Fm 3 (sel Fm hc), which says that there is an x0 such that for all x ≥ x0 and all indices i, with C' = sC' Fm and Cl = sCl Fm, the hypothesis AdmissibleBoundsFromSource.hyp (Fm.D x i) (Fm.L x i) 3 C' Cl (Fm.CYL + 1) (1/4) 3 (1/2) Fm.CTu implies that for all words u ≠ u', given Fm.x1 < x and (sel Fm hc).1 ≤ x, the squared norm of the K0 part of Y.tO u u' is at most (1 + 1/b^6) times duS u times duS u' divided by Dstar, where b is (Fm.L x i).sc.b.

RowNGP holds, meaning that for all reals Cg, cb, Cw, cT, CT, C0 with 0 < cb and 0 < cT there is a C4 ≥ 0 and there are thresholds C'₀ and Cl₀ such that for all C' ≥ C'₀ and Cl ≥ Cl₀, every D, large₂, X, Y and words u, u' satisfying Ties D, Hyp0 D large₂ C' Cl Cg cb Cw cT CT C0, Stand D u u', ConcTie X Y and AbsConv of Y.tO u u' also satisfy the condition RowNG of Y.tO u u' with arguments epsNG D large₂ C4 and ddC X Y u u'

RowsFinDim holds, meaning that for every AutInst I with a sigma-finite Haar measure μf, a fundamental domain fund, a right regular action R, a locally constant function e supported in I.Kset with convolution operator Re, and for unitary irreducible families σ with formal degrees dv, unit vectors w, integrable functions phLoc and an operator T that is the integral of R (g, 1) against phInf, the range of Re composed with T is finite dimensional over ℂ

for every eps, every Fm of type FamP eps, every proof hc of 𝒞 Fm, every x with Fm.x1 < x and (sel Fm hc).1 ≤ x and every index i in Fm.Ix x, LocTied (Fm.D x i) holds, meaning that for every finite place p of the base field there exists a LocIso between (Fm.D x i).s.atP p and locC (Fm.D x i) p

LoopRowS 3 𝒞 sel holds, meaning that for every function aF from lists of reals to reals, Closed 𝒞 holds for the property that for every hc there is an x0 such that for all x ≥ x0 and all i, with C' = sC' Fm and Cl = sCl Fm, for all words u, u' with Fm.x1 < x and (sel Fm hc).1 ≤ x, the hypothesis Cnt.Hyp (Fm.D x i) (Fm.L x i) u u' C' Cl (Fm.CYL + 1) (1/4) 3 (1/2) Fm.CTu 3 (aF Fm.cOut) together with ConcTie and AbsConv for the selected X and Y gives both RowBig and RowNotScalar of Y.tO u u' with arguments epsL (Fm.D x i) and ddC X Y u u'
second.conclusion: Closed 𝒞 holds for the property that every proof hc of 𝒞 Fm gives TheoremSSelected Fm 3 (sel Fm hc), which is an eventual bound on the squared norm of the K0 part of Y.tO u u' for distinct words u and u' by (1 + ((Fm.L x i).sc.b ^ 6)⁻¹) times duS u times duS u' divided by Dstar

deeper.says: The theorem assumes three global statements, called SWXS, RowNGP and RowsFinDim. It then takes any class 𝒞 of parameter families and any selector sel for that class, and it adds three more assumptions. The first is that every datum Fm.D x i of every family in 𝒞 satisfies LocTied whenever x exceeds the family's base point x1 and is at least the selected threshold. The second is the rank condition RanksRow with constant 3. The third is the row condition LoopRowS with constant 3 and the selector sel. Under these assumptions the property Closed holds for 𝒞. This means there is ε1 > 0 such that for every eps with 0 < eps ≤ ε1 there is a constant package K for which every family Fm in 𝒞 that is large with respect to K and any CH satisfies TheoremSSelected Fm 3 (sel Fm hc). TheoremSSelected says that for all large enough x and every index i, whenever AdmissibleBoundsFromSource.hyp holds for Fm.D x i and Fm.L x i with the constants 3, sC' Fm, sCl Fm, Fm.CYL + 1, 1/4, 3, 1/2 and Fm.CTu, and whenever Fm.x1 < x and s.1 ≤ x hold, then for any two distinct words u ≠ u' the squared norm of the quantity K0 of (s.2 x hx h0 i).Y.tO u u' is at most (1 + 1/b^6) · duS(u) · duS(u') / Dstar.
premises: SWXS holds, meaning that for every D of type D7 and every Hida setting X over D, the two opaque conditions SWa1 and StabilizerFirstChernCompatibility hold for the field, CM and Hermitian data of X

RowNGP holds, meaning that for all real constants Cg, cb, Cw, cT, CT, C0 with cb > 0 and cT > 0 there is C4 ≥ 0 and thresholds C'₀ and Cl₀ such that for all C' ≥ C'₀ and Cl ≥ Cl₀ and every D, size datum large₂, Hida setting X, full datum Y and words u, u', the conditions Ties D, Hyp0, Stand D u u', ConcTie X Y and AbsConv of Y.tO u u' together imply RowNG of Y.tO u u' with tolerance epsNG D large₂ C4 = 2^(−(k − 2·rS − 5)) · exp(C4 · mR(D)^5 · f · log b), where k − 2·rS − 5 is a subtraction of natural numbers that is cut off at zero, so the first factor is 1 whenever k < 2·rS + 5 and with the number ddC X Y u u' = duC(u) · duC(u') / DstC

RowsFinDim holds, meaning that for every record I of type AutInst, every σ-finite Haar measure μf on I.Gf, every subset fund of I.GA with I.IsFundDom (I.muA μf) fund, every map R on I.GA with I.IsRightReg μf fund R, every locally constant complex function e on I.Gf that vanishes outside I.Kset with an operator Re satisfying I.IsRConvF μf fund R e Re, and every family over the infinite places v of I.F of complex Hilbert spaces H v, maps σ v satisfying IsURepOn and IsIrredOn on UJset (I.ε v), reals dv v satisfying IsFdeg for muG (I.ε v), unit vectors w v and integrable functions phLoc (σ v) (w v) (dv v), every continuous linear operator T on I.L2 μf fund that satisfies IsOpInt with the measure muInf I, the action g ↦ R (g, 1) and the function phInf I σ w dv has a finite-dimensional complex space HH I μf fund Re T
a class 𝒞 of parameter families is given (a class is a property of families FamP eps for each real eps)
a selector sel for 𝒞 is given, which gives every family Fm in 𝒞 a pair made of a threshold x0 and, for each x > x1 with x ≥ x0 and each index i, an object of the opaque type STies for D x i

for every eps, every family Fm in 𝒞, every x with x1 < x and (sel Fm hc).1 ≤ x and every index i, the datum D x i satisfies LocTied, meaning that for every nonzero prime p of the ring of integers of the field host.F there exists a LocIso between the local datum (D.s.atP p) and the local datum locC D p that Examples₂.locAtC builds
RanksRow 3 𝒞 holds, meaning that Closed holds for 𝒞 with the property RanksF Fm 3 (Fm.CYL + 1) (1/4) 3 (1/2) Fm.CTu, which unfolds to the opaque FamilyRanksHypothesis

LoopRowS 3 𝒞 sel holds, meaning that for every function aF from real lists to reals, Closed holds for 𝒞 with the property that for every hc, eventually in x, for all indices and all words u, u', the hypothesis Hyp with C0 = 3 and A = aF(Fm.cOut), together with ConcTie and AbsConv for the selected data, implies both RowBig and RowNotScalar of Y.tO u u' with tolerance epsL = exp(−(1/3) · k · f · log k) and number ddC
deeper.conclusion: Closed holds for 𝒞 with the property that every family Fm in 𝒞, for every proof hc of membership, satisfies TheoremSSelected Fm 3 (sel Fm hc), which says that there is x0 such that for every x ≥ x0 and every index i, whenever AdmissibleBoundsFromSource.hyp holds for Fm.D x i and Fm.L x i with the constants 3, sC' Fm, sCl Fm, Fm.CYL + 1, 1/4, 3, 1/2 and Fm.CTu, and Fm.x1 < x and (sel Fm hc).1 ≤ x hold, the bound ‖K0(u,u')‖² ≤ (1 + 1/b^6) · duS(u) · duS(u') / Dstar holds for all distinct words u ≠ u'.
deeper.notation: SWXS ⇒ RowNGP ⇒ RowsFinDim ⇒ ∀ 𝒞 ∀ sel ∈ SSel(𝒞), [∀ eps ∀ Fm ∈ 𝒞 ∀ x > Fm.x1 with sel(Fm).1 ≤ x ∀ i, LocTied(Fm.D x i)] ⇒ RanksRow(3,𝒞) ⇒ LoopRowS(3,𝒞,sel) ⇒ ∃ ε1 > 0 ∀ eps ∈ (0, ε1] ∃ K ∀ Fm ∈ FamP(eps) ∀ CH, (𝒞 Fm ∧ Fm.Large K CH) ⇒ ∀ hc : 𝒞 Fm, ∃ x0 ∀ x ≥ x0 ∀ i, [hyp(D x i, L x i, 3, sC', sCl, CYL+1, 1/4, 3, 1/2, CTu) ⇒ (Fm.x1 < x ∧ sel(Fm,hc).1 ≤ x) ⇒ ∀ u ≠ u', ‖K0(Y.tO u u')‖² ≤ (1 + b⁻⁶) · duS(u) · duS(u') / Dstar]

deeper.suggests: As a suggestion only, the names point to an off-diagonal bound for a kernel K0 between distinct words in a relative trace or period computation for unitary groups, derived from local-global ties, rank bounds and row nondegeneracy, with the bound tending to the product duS(u)·duS(u')/Dstar as b grows.
deeper.why: The quantifier structure, the explicit constants and the bodies of Closed, TheoremSSelected, LoopRowS, RanksRow, LocTied and LocAt are all visible, but the key quantities and conditions K0, tO, RowBig, RowNG, Large, STies, StandingHypotheses and FamilyRanksHypothesis have no body in the files.

lines.name: GlobalTheory.Svd.servH_row_of_artin
lines.says: Assume the proposition that the code calls GlobalArtinReciprocity, which says that for every number field E with an algebraic closure Ω there is a monoid homomorphism art from Ideles E to Gab E Ω satisfying a condition that the code calls IsGlobalArtin. Then for every boundary type Bd, slot Q, linkage Lk and every function ker that assigns a KerEntTied record to each boundary element, if Q always implies the slot positionOf HasPart and if RowE Q Lk holds for the family that asks StdTie D O (ker D O c b), then Row Q Lk (ServH ker) holds. The dossier also folds five wrapper theorems into this line, and this reading does not describe them.
premises: GlobalArtinReciprocity holds, that is, for every number field E and algebraic closure Ω of E there exists a monoid homomorphism art from Ideles E to Gab E Ω with IsGlobalArtin art
Bd is any function that gives a type for each datum D, object O of D and real c, Q is any slot, Lk is any linkage for Bd, and ker gives a KerEntTied O.ex for each D, O, c and element of Bd D O c
for all K, X, f, T and c, the statement Q K X f T c implies positionOf HasPart K X f T c
RowE Q Lk E holds for the family E that sends any parameter and D, O, c, b to the statement StdTie D O (ker D O c b)
lines.conclusion: Row Q Lk (ServH ker) holds, that is, there is a family E with RowE Q Lk E such that every class 𝒜 and raw selection σ satisfying IsSel Q Lk E 𝒜 σ also satisfies ServH ker 𝒜 σ
lines.notation: GlobalArtinReciprocity ⇒ ∀ Bd ∀ Q ∀ Lk ∀ ker, [∀ K X f T c, Q K X f T c ⇒ positionOf HasPart K X f T c] ⇒ RowE Q Lk ((_, D, O, c, b) ↦ StdTie D O (ker D O c b)) ⇒ Row Q Lk (ServH ker), where Row Q Lk H means ∃ E, RowE Q Lk E ∧ ∀ 𝒜 ∀ σ, IsSel Q Lk E 𝒜 σ ⇒ H 𝒜 σ, and RowE Q Lk E means EvP ((κ, K) ↦ ∀ β ∈ BPt K, β.Is Q ⇒ ∀ c ∈ ℝ ∀ b ∈ Bd β.D β.O c, Lk K β c b ⇒ E κ β.D β.O c b), and ServH ker 𝒜 σ means Closed 𝒜 ((Fm, _) ↦ RowTwU Fm) ∧ AtAll ((D, O, c, b) ↦ Pdv.At O.ex (ker D O c b).ent) 𝒜 σ

terms.name: GlobalArtinReciprocity
terms.gloss: The dossier shows this to be the proposition that for every number field E and algebraic closure Ω there exists a monoid homomorphism art from Ideles E to Gab E Ω satisfying IsGlobalArtin, where Ideles, Gab and IsGlobalArtin have no visible bodies.

terms.name: BdT
terms.gloss: The dossier shows this to be the type of functions that assign a type to each datum D, object O of D and real number.

terms.name: LkT
terms.gloss: The dossier shows a linkage for Bd to be a function that assigns a true or false statement to each context K, point β of BPt K, real c and element of Bd β.D β.O c.

terms.name: Slot
terms.gloss: The dossier shows a slot to be a function that assigns a true or false statement to each context K, stages X, frame f, twisting datum T and element of Core K X f T.

terms.name: Obj
terms.gloss: The dossier shows an object of D to be a record of size data L, tie data gatT, instances Gx and Gy, constants K, a DivX record X, constants cX and an Extra record ex built from all of these.

terms.name: KerEntTied
terms.gloss: The dossier shows this to be a long record over an Extra record ex that holds an ideal cc equal to D.host.ccK, a complex number δ, a function χ, fields X, primes, characters, lift objects O u μ, a KerEnt record ent and many equations that tie these to D and ex.

terms.name: positionOf
terms.gloss: The dossier shows positionOf P to be the slot that holds at K, X, f, T, c when there are w, Z and c' with P K X.B f T w Z c' such that the triple made from X.C, the later stages of X and c equals the triple (w.C, Z, c').

terms.name: HasPart
terms.gloss: The dossier shows HasPart to hold at w, Z, c when a type that the code calls Part w Z c.O has at least one element.

terms.name: RowE
terms.gloss: The dossier shows RowE Q Lk E to be a condition that the code calls EvP applied to the statement that for every point β with β.Is Q, every real c and every b in Bd β.D β.O c, the linkage Lk K β c b implies E κ β.D β.O c b.

terms.name: Row

Q is any slot predicate of type V4.Slot. Such a predicate takes a context K, stages X, a frame f, twist data T and a core c, and returns a proposition.

Lk is any predicate of type LkT Bd. It takes a context K, an element β of type BPt K, a real number c and an element of Bd β.D β.O c, and returns a proposition. Here Lk is a bound variable and not the definition Formalism.L2.Forms.Lk.

deeper.says: The theorem says that the proposition the code calls mainTheorem holds, and that proposition is one long implication. It assumes four bundles of named statements, called Hypotheses₂, PublishedInputsThirdLayerAlt, GeometricGaloisRepCompatibility and SerN. It also assumes the depth-zero support statement DepthZeroSupport and three statements called LocalFiniteness, LocalTateDuality and LocalEulerChar, each of which says that a per-place condition with no visible body holds for every finite ZMod(l^r)-representation of Dec A at every finite place of every number field. Under these assumptions, it says that for every proof hL of the statement RecTExists and every real number cDep, take the parameter record p = parametersOfDependence hL cDep. If LinkedAt holds for p with the row test built from Closed and BoundAtTwoThreeFamilyFonAlt, then LinkedAt also holds for p with the same row test built from Closed and LinkN. In other words, the theorem transfers a linkage statement from the bound condition BoundAtTwoThreeFamilyFonAlt to the condition LinkN, at the same parameters and in the same row and slot setting, and it does not claim that either linkage holds outright.

deeper.says: The theorem says that if the large bundle of hypotheses called UnitaryGroupThirdPlaceHypotheses holds, then two statements both hold. The first statement, SurjectiveOntoX, says the following. deeper.says: The theorem is a chain of twelve implications. If twelve propositions all hold, then the proposition that the code calls SurjectiveOntoX holds. Each of the twelve is a closed statement that the code files under the label Published or under UpperTheory, such as a Chebotarev statement with degree-one primes, a statement named after Clozel that for every π of type CuspSub E a the condition IsRegAlg of CG.mk π implies the condition GKCoh.IsCohomological π, a Bhatt–Scholze statement on crystalline lattices, a Casselman–Wallach statement, and an existence statement for maps rc satisfying the condition IsRecT. There is a threshold ε₁ > 0 such that, for every eps with 0 < eps ≤ ε₁, there is an object K of the type the code calls TransportedAlt with this property. deeper.says: The theorem says that if the hypothesis bundle the code calls UnitaryGroupThirdPlaceHypotheses holds, then a conclusion follows for every proof hL of the proposition RecTExists and for every real number cDep. RecTExists says that for every number field E, every algebraic closure Ω of E, every valuation subring A of Ω and every nonzero prime w of the ring of integers of E that A lies over, there is a map rc that satisfies a condition the code calls IsRecT. The hypothesis bundle is the joint assertion of a long list of named statements, most of them in the namespace Published, such as BernsteinUnitaryProductIrreducible, ChebotarevDegreeOne, which gives for every finite set S of primes a prime outside S of inertia degree 1 with a Frobenius condition IsFrob, and GlobalArtinReciprocity. The conclusion is that the parameter record parametersOfDependence hL cDep satisfies OpenParameterStatements. This means that twelve row or slot conditions each hold in the sense the code calls LinkedAt for that record.

deeper.says: Assume fourteen propositions that the code names after published results, from HarishChandraFinite through the second proposition called SiegelWeilUnitaryConvergent, which lives in the HeckeCharacterZeroLocus namespace. Then for every proof hL of the statement RecTExists, every norm-choice extension N over hL, every S of type SExt and every geometric predicate Γ of type GeoP, two claims hold for the parameter record p = parametersOfExtension N S Γ, which is the four-part record made of RX, N, S and Γ. The first claim is LinkedAt p r, where r takes a slot Q and a linkage L to the proposition Row Q L (AtAll R). Here R is the test that, for a bundle b, holds when the condition MIstar2 holds for the complex datum b.B.Q.Rl.toCx3 b.B.Q.F, with arguments b.B.Q.F.eV applied to that datum's zs and b.B.Q.sEE. The second claim is LinkedAt p RowMultiplicityCondition, which is the same row statement with the test wrapped by an operator the code calls Ind.EvW in place of AtAll. Unfolded, each claim says that there is a slot R0 such that a condition the code calls LargeBaseCondition holds for KPx, IsBuiltE p.s and R0, and such that the row statement holds at the slot that is the pointwise conjunction of IsGoodE p.s with R0, paired with the linkage BundleLinkage p.

deeper.notation: HCFinite ⇒ CuspRapidDecay ⇒ DSCover ⇒ HCModules ⇒ CasselmanWallach ⇒ HoweUnram ⇒ WeilRepPair ⇒ WeilSiegel ⇒ SWConv ⇒ DoublingZeta ⇒ UnramDoublingGL ⇒ DSClass ⇒ StrongApproxSU ⇒ SWConv′ ⇒ ∀ hL ∈ RecTExists, ∀ N ∈ NormChoiceExtension(hL), ∀ S ∈ SExt, ∀ Γ ∈ GeoP, with p = ⟨RX, N, S, Γ⟩ we have LinkedAt(p, (Q,L) ↦ [∃ E, RowE(Q,L,E) ∧ ∀ 𝒜 σ, IsSel(Q,L,E,𝒜,σ) ⇒ ∀ ε, ∀ Fm ∈ 𝒜, ∀ x > Fm.x1, ∀ i ∈ Fm.Ix(x), R(σ(Fm,hc,x,hx,i))]) ∧ LinkedAt(p, RowMultiplicityCondition), where LinkedAt(p, r) ⇔ ∃ R0, LargeBaseCondition(KPx, IsBuiltE(p.s), R0) ∧ r(IsGoodE(p.s) ∧ R0, BundleLinkage(p)) and RowMultiplicityCondition(Q,L) ⇔ ∃ E, RowE(Q,L,E) ∧ ∀ 𝒜 σ, IsSel(Q,L,E,𝒜,σ) ⇒ EvW(R)(𝒜,σ), where R(b) ⇔ MIstar2(toCx3(b.B.Q.Rl, b.B.Q.F), eV(b.B.Q.F, toCx3(b.B.Q.Rl, b.B.Q.F).zs), b.B.Q.sEE) and hc and hx are the proofs of Fm ∈ 𝒜 and of x > Fm.x1
deeper.suggests: As a suggestion only, the names hint at the following reading. The premises would be published theorems of automorphic representation theory, such as Harish-Chandra finiteness, Casselman–Wallach, the Siegel–Weil formula and strong approximation, taken as hypotheses. The conclusion would then say that the bundles produced by the theta-lift construction satisfy an isometric-period unit condition MIstar2 at every index, and eventually in the sense of EvW, so that the row multiplicity condition holds.
deeper.why: The logical shape is visible through LinkedAt, Row and AtAll, but the core conditions MIstar2 internals, RowE, IsSel, EvW, LargeBaseCondition and RX have no visible body, so the mathematical content of the conclusion cannot be seen.

terms.name: RowE
terms.gloss: The dossier shows RowE Q Lk E as EvP of the statement that for every point β of type BPt K with β.Is Q, every real c and every bundle b with Lk K β c b, the property E κ β.D β.O c b holds.

terms.name: EvP
terms.gloss: The dossier shows EvP P as ParEv of the statement that if κ.Pos then there is a real x0 such that P κ K holds for every context K with κ.Of K and x0 ≤ K.s.x, where ParEv, Pos and Of have no bodies here.

terms.name: MIstar2
terms.gloss: It appears only as a property applied to objects projected from the field B.Q of a bundle b, and the dossier shows no body for it or for the projections Rl, F, toCx3, eV, zs and sEE.

terms.name: RowDiag
terms.gloss: The dossier shows RowDiag E as Core.Rk.Row E applied to the property SDiag D u L C.

terms.name: Core.Rk.Row
terms.gloss: The dossier shows Row E Q as the statement that for all reals Cg, cb, Cu, cT, CT with 0 < cb and 0 < cT there are reals C, C'₀, Cl₀ with 1 ≤ C such that for all C' ≥ C'₀ and Cl ≥ Cl₀ and all D, L, u, the conditions TrueE D, E D L C' and HD D L C' Cl Cg cb Cu cT CT together give Q D u L C.

terms.name: SDiag
terms.gloss: The dossier shows SDiag D u L C as a condition TwoTerm D u applied to the two numbers 4(exp(C · mfL D L) + 1) and 4 exp(−kfk D / 2) + 2 exp(−kfk D), where TwoTerm, mfL and kfk have no bodies here.

terms.name: IsScaleWithBoundedGamma
terms.gloss: The dossier shows it as the statement that some size record of type SizeData₂ D has scale field sc.L equal to L, has 8 times its field CGam at most C', and has CGam at least 1.

terms.name: RankMu
terms.gloss: The dossier shows RankMu D u as the equation that d0 D u equals (D.mem u).A.duStar times the quantity ((D.mem u).A.T to the power D.R.k, minus 1) raised to the power D.R.f.

terms.name: d0
terms.gloss: The dossier shows d0 D u as the dimension over the complex numbers of a space written D.s.Cu u.

terms.name: TrueE, HD
terms.gloss: These appear as side conditions inside Core.Rk.Row and the dossier shows no bodies for them.

terms.name: BundleLinkage
terms.gloss: The dossier shows it as linkOf of the property that BundleWitness q b is nonempty, so that a bundle b at β is linked when some point p' of type WPt and bundle b' with a witness give the same triple of D, O and bundle as β and b.

terms.name: BundleWitness
terms.gloss: The dossier shows it as a record with fifteen fields that tie the bundle b to data of the point q, mostly by equalities and by conditions with names that have no bodies here.

terms.name: IsGoodE
terms.gloss: The dossier shows IsGoodE 𝒮 as positionOf (GoodE 𝒮), and neither inner name has a body here.

terms.name: Parameters
terms.gloss: The dossier shows it as a record with four fields named R, N, S and Γ, and the projection p.s used in the statement is not among the shown fields.

terms.name: WPt
terms.gloss: The dossier shows WPt 𝒮 K as a record with fields B, f, T, w, Z, O and x, where x has type Wit 𝒮 K w Z (ofObj O).

terms.name: RXs
terms.gloss: The dossier shows it as a record with seventeen fields of compatibility data and conditions for a row object t, including a rank condition 1 ≤ p + q for each j.

terms.name: Ctx
terms.gloss: The dossier shows it as a record with a scale s, constants C, cD, ch, data P, q1, integer functions a and b, a Boolean function c, and several conditions and equalities.

terms.name: BPt
terms.gloss: The dossier shows BPt K as a record with fields X, f, T, c, Y and eleven further conditions that tie it to the context K, and the projections β.D, β.O and β.Is are not among the shown fields.

terms.name: RecTExists

lines.suggests: The names suggest that this is the closing step for a multiplicity (MI star) row, which shows that for all large enough scales every good point with a linked bundle has the multiplicity property, given published analytic inputs, a diagonal two-term estimate and the existence of certain row data at every weighted point, but the dossier does not show this.
lines.why: The premises RowDiag, IsScaleWithBoundedGamma and RankMu and the shape of RowE and EvP are visible, but MIstar2, ParEv, TwoTerm, HD, the projections β.Is and p.s and 140 left out definitions keep the core content opaque.

deeper.says: The theorem says that if fourteen given statements all hold, then a certain conclusion holds for every proof hL of the statement the code calls RecTExists and for every parameter record p built over hL. The first thirteen are statements from the GlobalTheory.Published and GlobalTheory.Hk3 namespaces, such as HarishChandraFinite, CasselmanWallach, WeilSiegelFormulaUnitary and StrongApproxSU. The fourteenth is RowDiag applied to a predicate E. Here E D L C' holds when D has size data whose scale has L as its field L and whose constant CGam satisfies 1 ≤ CGam and 8·CGam ≤ C', and when for every word u the complex dimension of the space D.s.Cu u equals duStar·(T^k − 1)^f. For each such hL and p there is one more premise, namely that for every context K and every point q of type WPt p.s K the record type RXs q.x.what₂ has an element. The conclusion is RowE for the slot IsGoodE p.s and the linkage BundleLinkage p, with a target predicate that requires MIstar2 to hold for the data read off each linked bundle b.

terms.name: RowE
terms.gloss: For a slot Q, a linkage Lk and a property E, it says that EvP holds of the statement that every point β of BPt K with β.Is Q, every real c and every bundle b linked to β by Lk satisfy E.

terms.name: EvP
terms.gloss: For a predicate p on pairs (κ, K), it says that ParEv holds of the statement that if κ.Pos then there is a real x0 such that p κ K holds for every context K with κ.Of K and x0 ≤ K.s.x, where ParEv, Pos and Of are not shown.

terms.name: RowDiag
terms.gloss: For a condition E it is Row E Q with Q(D, u, L, C) equal to SDiag D u L C.

terms.name: Row
terms.gloss: It says that for all reals Cg, cb, Cu, cT, CT with 0 < cb and 0 < cT there exist reals C, C'₀, Cl₀ with 1 ≤ C such that for all C' ≥ C'₀ and Cl ≥ Cl₀ and all D, L, u, the conditions TrueE D, E D L C' and HD D L C' Cl Cg cb Cu cT CT together imply Q D u L C, where TrueE and HD are not shown.

terms.name: SDiag
terms.gloss: It is the condition TwoTerm D u (4(exp(C · mfL D L) + 1)) (4 exp(−kfk D / 2) + 2 exp(−kfk D)), where TwoTerm, mfL and kfk are not shown.

terms.name: IsScaleWithBoundedGamma
terms.gloss: It says that there is a size datum large₂ for D whose scale has L-value equal to L, with 8 · CGam ≤ C' and 1 ≤ CGam.

terms.name: RankMu
terms.gloss: It says that the complex dimension d0 D u of the space D.s.Cu u equals duStar times (T^k − 1)^f, with duStar and T taken from the member D.mem u and k and f taken from D.R.

terms.name: BundlePointConditions
terms.gloss: It is a bundle of ten conditions on a bundle b, most of them opaque, which include a gap condition GapGe with bound 100 · r⁴ and the inequality 1 ≤ D.R.rS.

terms.name: MIstar2
terms.gloss: It is a condition attached to the object toCx3 whose body the dossier does not show.

terms.name: BundleLinkage
terms.gloss: It is the linkage built by linkOf from the relation that says a BundleWitness for q and b exists, where linkOf and BundleWitness are not shown.

terms.name: IsGoodE
terms.gloss: It is the slot positionOf (GoodE 𝒮), where positionOf and GoodE are not shown.

terms.name: Parameters
terms.gloss: It is a record with four fields R, N, S and Γ of types RPosition, NormChoiceExtension hL, SExt and GeoP, and the projection p.s used in the statement is not among the shown fields.

terms.name: WPt
terms.gloss: It is a record made of a base B, data f, T, w, Z, an object O and a witness x of type Wit 𝒮 K w Z (ofObj O).

terms.name: RXs
terms.gloss: It is a record of data and conditions attached to a row object t, with nineteen fields that rest on names not shown.

terms.name: RecTExists
terms.gloss: It says that for every number field E with algebraic closure Ω, every valuation subring A of Ω, every finite place w of E and every proof h of IsPlaceOver A w, there is an rc with IsRecT h rc.

terms.name: the thirteen published propositions

terms.name: DoublingMethodLocalZetaIntegrals

lines.says: The theorem is a chain of fifteen implications. If fifteen named propositions all hold, each taken here as a hypothesis, then the proposition that the code calls CovolumeBoundOfX holds. CovolumeBoundOfX is shown to say that a condition the code calls Closed holds for an object called FamHyp and for the following property of a pair (Fm, CH), namely that there is a real number C0 with 0 ≤ C0 such that a condition called EventuallyAtAllPoints holds for Fm and for the property of p which says that for every real C with C0 ≤ C a condition called L3, attached to p.S false, holds of p.N C CH.
premises: ResolutionCharZero holds, which says that every reduced scheme X with a locally finite type, quasi-compact, separated map g to the spectrum of a field k of characteristic zero has a map s from some X' to X that satisfies a condition called IsBlowupSeq, makes the composite to Sp k smooth, is an isomorphism over the smooth locus of g, and makes the object that the code calls preRed, formed from s and the closed complement of the smooth locus, satisfy a condition called Snc

PrincipalisationCharZero holds, which says that for X smooth of relative dimension d, quasi-compact and separated over a field k of characteristic zero, an ideal sheaf I whose support contains no irreducible component of X, and a closed set E whose vanishing ideal satisfies SncAt at each point of E, there are X', a map s from X' to X and a closed set E' with IsSncBlowupSeq g E s E', with the composite to Sp k smooth, with the pullback of I satisfying EffCartier, with the vanishing ideal of its support satisfying Snc, and with s an isomorphism away from the support of I

PoincareLelongInv holds, which is an identity between quantities called ptsIntegral, stating that the integral of logNorm A s on P against the potentials log B.h and log (L j).h equals a finite sum over the horizontal members W of divSupp P s of the multiplicity multAt (P + (s)) W times the integral of log B.h on W against the potentials log (L j).h, minus the integral of log B.h on P against log A.h and the potentials log (L j).h, under smoothness and conjugation-invariance premises on the L j, A and B, with B.a = 0, IsArithVar P (n + 2) and IsSectionOn P A s
HSUse holds, which is the conjunction of three propositions that the code calls ArithKleiman.Statement, G7.Statement and ArithmeticVolumeNef.Statement

MoriwakiBigStatement holds, which says that under eight listed conditions on a coordinate tuple y, a Hermitian datum A, an ideal P0 and an intersection system II, the number II K ι (mCoordIdeal y) (D + 1) (constant family A) is at most a quantity called arVolP (IsSmallH (mCoordIdeal y) y A) (chartLat y A.a) 1 D

FarguesExact holds, which says that for a prime p, an algebraically closed valued field C of characteristic zero with ring of integers O that is p-adically complete and has v(p) < 1, a PDivGroup G over O, a compatible system ζ of p-power roots with ζ(0) = 1 and ζ(1) ≠ 1, and any O-bilinear form B that matches the map called pairing, an element x has hodgeTateLinear G x = 0 exactly when B x y = 0 for every y with dlogLinear G y = 0

ZarhinStatement holds, which says that every abelian scheme A with a relatively ample line bundle datum over the spectrum of the ring of integers R of a valued algebraically closed field admits an object P of type PolAV over the same base and maps i from A to P.A and r from P.A to A, both satisfying IsMonHom, with i followed by r equal to the identity of A

SiegelToroidalIntegral holds, which says that for every g ≥ 1 there is a function φ with IsPolFan id g φ such that for every odd n ≥ 3 there exist a family F, a scheme S projective and smooth of relative dimension g(g+1)/2 over Sp (cycAway n), an open immersion j of F.X into S, a semi-abelian group object G over S smooth of relative dimension g, and further data BD, d ≥ 1 and N ≥ 1 that satisfy thirteen listed conditions, the last of which is an ampleness condition IsAmpleLB for all k from some k₀ on

ToroidalForFanKS holds, which says that for a CM number field E with data H, Dw with 1 ≤ Dw.p + Dw.q, a function φ with IsPolFan and NoSelfInt, a level l, a moduli object Xo and a coefficient object c, there exist a Model Y, a datum BD and naturals d ≥ 1 and k ≥ 1 that satisfy six listed conditions, among them smoothness of relative dimension Dw.dim, Snc of a boundary ideal, HasChartOf at boundary points, a conditional ampleness, and HasLogKS

SemiAbelianLieSeminegative holds, which says that over a scheme C that is smooth of relative dimension 1, projective and geometrically connected over a field k of characteristic zero, for a semi-abelian group object G over C and a module W with IsVB W r and a monomorphism from W to Lie G, the number interNum k (structureModule C) [det W r] is at most 0

PointSeparationPair holds, which says that on an integral, locally Noetherian, normal scheme X projective over the complex numbers of dimension n, under listed conditions on a line bundle datum M, a function Δ, data m, G, r, N₀, two distinct closed points x₁ and x₂ and positive reals c(e) with the sum over e from 1 to n of 2^(1/e) · e / c(e) at most 1, there is a section s of M whose nonzero locus contains exactly one of x₁ and x₂

lines.conclusion: the proposition that the code calls CovolumeBoundOfX holds, which is the condition Closed applied to FamHyp and to the property that some C0 ≥ 0 exists for which EventuallyAtAllPoints Fm holds of the statement that L3 holds at p.N C CH for every C ≥ C0

terms.name: Datum
terms.gloss: A Datum for a Host is a finitely generated projective module La over the integers of E of rank p + q, with an alternating integer bilinear form EF that is bijective as a map to the dual and satisfies EF(a·x, y) = EF(x, bar(a)·y), together with natural numbers p and q and the existence of a real linear map J with J² = −1 that satisfies positivity and trace conditions written in terms of p, q and the embeddings sending rt to rt0.

lines.says: Assume three things, namely a condition bundle that the code calls OpenImageCondition, a statement called BaseChangeIsobaricN, and a statement called RowT. Then the statement VWin holds, which says that for every primitive complex Dirichlet character ψ the window statement VWinAt ψ 401 holds. VWinAt ψ 401 says that for every real eps with 0 < eps < 1/52 and every function e from the reals to the natural numbers with PageN eps x (e x) for all x ≥ 1, there are a real J ≥ 1 and a real X0 such that for every X ≥ X0 and every pair of natural numbers q, d with WinPair eps (X^(1/J)) q d, some real Y with X^(1/J) ≤ Y and Y² ≤ X has VAt ψ eps 401 q d (e x) x for every x between Y and Y².
premises: OpenImageCondition holds, which the dossier shows to be a bundle with one field, and that field is exactly the statement RowT

BaseChangeIsobaricN holds, which says that for every CM number field E in which every finite prime is unramified over the ring of integers of the maximal real subfield, every n ≥ 1 and every space π of complex functions on the group UA E n satisfying IsAutRepU, there exist a number c, sizes N_1,…,N_c adding up to n, and further data V, σ, m, P satisfying a condition that the code calls IsBaseChangeN

RowT holds, which is Row0b applied to the notion IsRecT, and which says that for every CM number field E with algebraic closure Ω, every prime l, every ring isomorphism ι from Qbar l to ℂ, every a ≥ 1, every π of type CuspSub E a and every χ of type HChar on the maximal real subfield, if CG.mk π satisfies IsRegAlg and PolarizedPair π χ holds then there exist a group homomorphism r from G E Ω to GL_a(Qbar l), an integer wt and a function HT satisfying a condition that the code calls PropsB
lines.conclusion: VWin holds, that is, VWinAt ψ 401 holds for every primitive Dirichlet character ψ
lines.notation: OpenImageCondition ∧ BaseChangeIsobaricN ∧ RowT ⇒ VWin, where VWin ⇔ ∀ ψ ∈ PChar, ∀ eps ∈ ℝ, 0 < eps < 1/52 ⇒ ∀ e ∈ (ℝ → ℕ), (∀ x ≥ 1, PageN(eps, x, e(x))) ⇒ ∃ J ≥ 1, ∃ X0 ∈ ℝ, ∀ X ≥ X0, ∀ q, d ∈ ℕ, WinPair(eps, X^(1/J), q, d) ⇒ ∃ Y ∈ ℝ, X^(1/J) ≤ Y ∧ Y² ≤ X ∧ ∀ x ∈ ℝ, Y ≤ x ≤ Y² ⇒ VAt(ψ, eps, 401, q, d, e(x), x)

lines.says: With no premises, the statement Row0b holds for the notion recT, which is the notion IsRecT. In words, for every CM number field E with an algebraic closure Ω, every prime l, every ring isomorphism ι from an algebraic closure of the l-adic numbers to ℂ, every a ≥ 1, every π of type CuspSub E a and every χ of type HChar on the maximal real subfield of E, if the class of π satisfies IsRegAlg and the pair satisfies PolarizedPair π χ, then there exist a group homomorphism r from the automorphism group of Ω over E to GL_a over the l-adic algebraic closure, an integer wt, and a function HT assigning a multiset of integers to each field embedding of E into the l-adic algebraic closure, such that PropsB recT π ι r wt HT holds. PropsB asserts that r is continuous, that r satisfies IsSSRep, a condition AwayB at each finite prime not containing l, two explicit identities for HT, and a condition AboveB.
lines.conclusion: Row0b recT holds, that is, every π over a CM field with IsRegAlg and PolarizedPair has some r, wt and HT with PropsB recT π ι r wt HT
lines.notation: ∀ E CM number field, ∀ Ω algebraic closure of E, ∀ l prime, ∀ ι ∈ (Qbar_l ≅ ℂ as rings), ∀ a ≥ 1, ∀ π ∈ CuspSub(E, a), ∀ χ ∈ HChar(E⁺), IsRegAlg([π]) ∧ PolarizedPair(π, χ) ⇒ ∃ r ∈ Hom(Aut_E(Ω), GL_a(Qbar_l)), ∃ wt ∈ ℤ, ∃ HT ∈ ((E → Qbar_l) → Multisets(ℤ)), PropsB(recT, π, ι, r, wt, HT). Inside PropsB, r is continuous ∧ IsSSRep(r) ∧ (∀ w ∌ l, ∀ A, ∀ h ∈ IsPlaceOver(A, w), ∀ rc, IsRecT(h, rc) ⇒ ∀ σ, IsLocComp(π, w, σ) ⇒ AwayB(wdOf(h, ι, r), rc(algNorm σ))) ∧ (∀ τ, HT(τ) = {(a − 1)/2 − z, z ∈ infChar([π], ι∘τ)} as multisets in ℂ) ∧ (∀ τ, HT(τ∘c) = {wt − n, n ∈ HT(τ)}, c complex conjugation of E) ∧ (∀ P, AI, LocTied(l, P, AI) nonempty ⇒ ∀ w, A, h, O, Bw, hj, AboveB(recT, π, ι, r, HT, P, h, Bw, hj))

second.says: With no premises, the theorem states Row0b for the notion recT, where recT sends h and rc to IsRecT h rc, which says that there exist a and ha with the condition that the code calls LawsT a ha rc. Spelled out, for every CM number field E with algebraic closure Ω, every prime l, every ring isomorphism ι from Qbar l (the algebraic closure of the l-adic numbers) to ℂ, every a ≥ 1, every π in CuspSub E a and every χ in HChar of the maximal real subfield of E such that (CG.mk π).IsRegAlg holds and PolarizedPair π χ holds (meaning χ.locInf v (-1) = (-1)^a at every infinite place v of the maximal real subfield, and DualIsConjBy π (compNorm E χ)), there exist a group homomorphism r from the group G E Ω of E-algebra automorphisms of Ω to GL of size a over Qbar l, an integer wt and a function HT from embeddings of E into Qbar l to multisets of integers with PropsB recT π ι r wt HT. PropsB says that r is continuous, that IsSSRep r holds, that at each finite place w not containing l, for each A with IsPlaceOver A w, each rc with recT h rc and each σ with π.IsLocComp w σ the condition AwayB (wdOf h hl ι r) (rc (algNorm σ)) holds, that for each τ the multiset HT τ read in ℂ equals the multiset infChar of CG.mk π at ι composed with τ mapped by z ↦ (a − 1)/2 − z, that HT of τ composed with complex conjugation equals HT τ mapped by n ↦ wt − n, and that the condition AboveB holds for all P, AI with LocTied l P AI nonempty and all w, A, h, O, Bw and hj.
second.conclusion: Row0b recT holds, that is every such pair π and χ over a CM field has a homomorphism r, an integer wt and a function HT satisfying PropsB with respect to recT
