premises: TLiftK holds, which says that for every CM number field E with maximal real subfield E⁺, every B of type Base with GoodK (cj E) B, every n ≥ 1 and every X of type Spc of size n with X.J = 1 and X.IsHerm (cj E) B n 0, there is a natural number d₀ such that for every d ≥ d₀, every W of type Spc of size d with W.J equal to δ times the identity matrix for some δ in E and W.IsSkew (cj E) B d 0, every pair of characters χX, χW satisfying IsHecke, ResEtaPow with exponents n and d respectively, and HasExp with integer families mX and mW, every space U of functions on UA E n with IsAutRepU U, and every family lam of weights with HasWeightAt U at each infinite place w and with d + mW(w) ≤ 2·lam(w)_k for all w and k, there exists a space U' of functions on UA E d with IsLift B χX χW mX mW lam U U'
lines.conclusion: Row0b recT holds, that is, every π over a CM field with IsRegAlg and PolarizedPair has some r, wt and HT with PropsB recT π ι r wt HT
lines.notation: TLiftK ⇒ Row0b(recT), where TLiftK ⇔ ∀ E CM, ∀ B ∈ Base(E⁺, E), GoodK(cj, B) ⇒ ∀ n ≥ 1, ∀ X ∈ Spc(n), X.J = 1 ⇒ IsHerm(X, cj, B, n, 0) ⇒ ∃ d₀ ∈ ℕ, ∀ d ≥ d₀, ∀ W ∈ Spc(d), ∀ δ ∈ E, W.J = δ·I_d ⇒ IsSkew(W, cj, B, d, 0) ⇒ ∀ χX, χW, mX, mW, IsHecke(χX) ⇒ IsHecke(χW) ⇒ ResEtaPow(K, χX, n) ⇒ ResEtaPow(K, χW, d) ⇒ HasExp(B.emb, χX, mX) ⇒ HasExp(B.emb, χW, mW) ⇒ ∀ U, ∀ lam, IsAutRepU(U) ⇒ (∀ w, HasWeightAt(U, B.emb(w), lam(w))) ⇒ (∀ w, k, d + mW(w) ≤ 2·lam(w)_k) ⇒ ∃ U', IsLift(B, χX, χW, mX, mW, lam, U, U'), with K the image of (E⁺)ˣ in the unit group of the adele ring of E⁺, and Row0b(recT) ⇔ ∀ E CM, Ω, l, ι, a ≥ 1, π, χ, IsRegAlg([π]) ∧ PolarizedPair(π, χ) ⇒ ∃ r, wt, HT, PropsB(recT, π, ι, r, wt, HT)

terms.name: TLiftK
terms.gloss: The universally quantified existence statement described in the premise, producing a space U' on a larger group of size d from a space U on a group of size n.

terms.name: IsLift
terms.gloss: A bundle saying that U' satisfies IsAutRepU, that at each infinite place U' has some weight lam' related to lam(w), mX(w), mW(w) by IsLiftWt, and that at each split place datum t any local components of U and U' given by CompAt are related by LocPair, where IsLiftWt, CompAt and LocPair have no visible bodies.

terms.name: GoodK
terms.gloss: A bundle of six conditions on a conjugation σ and a base datum B, saying IsCMExt, HasK, that the ring of integers of E is unramified over that of F, IsStd of B.ψ, a condition at inert places including 2 ∉ v, norm of v greater than 3 and PsiUnr, and PsiUnr at the places in B.P.

terms.name: Base
terms.gloss: A record holding an additive character ψ of the adele ring, a choice emb of embedding at each infinite place, two integer families mα and mβ, a finite set P of places with embeddings τ, and one further place v₁ with embedding τ₁.

terms.name: Spc
terms.gloss: A record holding an n by n matrix J over E, a lattice L in E^n over the ring of integers, a complex matrix θ at each infinite place, and an invertible matrix bas at each place.

terms.name: Chr
terms.gloss: The type of group homomorphisms from the units of a ring AE F E to the unit circle.

terms.name: IsHecke
terms.gloss: The statement that χ is continuous and takes the value 1 on the image of the units of E.

terms.name: ResEtaPow
terms.gloss: The statement that χ restricted to units a of the base ring equals 1 when a lies in the subgroup generated by K and the norms, and equals (−1)^n otherwise.

terms.name: HasExp
terms.gloss: The statement that on units z satisfying a closeness condition At (evI F) (z − 1), χ(z) equals the product over infinite places w of (z_w / |z_w|)^(m w).

terms.name: DomWeight
terms.gloss: A non-increasing sequence of N integers.

terms.name: IsAutRepU
terms.gloss: For a space of functions on UA E n, the bundle saying every member satisfies IsAutFormU, the space is stable under RU, is nonzero, and has no RU-stable subspaces other than zero and itself.

terms.name: HasWeightAt
terms.gloss: The statement IsCompAlong π (embU n τ) (…) (sqRep ℂ n lam), built from names whose bodies are not shown.

terms.name: IsHerm, IsSkew
terms.gloss: Two conditions on a Spc record that the theorem names but whose definitions are not shown.

terms.name: Row0b, recT, PropsB, CuspSub, PolarizedPair
terms.gloss: The same definitions as in line 33, shown with the same bodies.

terms.name: IsRegAlg, IsSSRep, AwayB, AboveB, LawsT
terms.gloss: Conditions inside Row0b and PropsB whose bodies are not shown.

lines.suggests: The names suggest that a theta lifting statement between unitary groups of sizes n and d, for all sufficiently large d, is enough to construct the Galois representations of line 33.
lines.why: Both the premise and the conclusion have fully visible quantifier structure, but the key conditions IsHerm, IsSkew, IsLiftWt, LocPair, HasWeightAt, IsRegAlg, AwayB and AboveB are opaque.

second.says: Given a proof up of TLiftK, the statement Row0b recT holds, which is the same conclusion as in line 33 (for every CM number field E with algebraic closure Ω, prime l, isomorphism ι from Qbar l to ℂ, a ≥ 1, π in CuspSub E a and χ in HChar of the maximal real subfield with (CG.mk π).IsRegAlg and PolarizedPair π χ, there exist r, wt and HT with PropsB recT π ι r wt HT). TLiftK says that for every CM number field E with maximal real subfield F and every B in Base F E with W.GoodK (cj E) B, every n ≥ 1 and every X in Spc F E n with X.J = 1 and X.IsHerm (cj E) B n 0, there is a d₀ such that for every d ≥ d₀, every W in Spc F E d and δ in E with W.J = δ times the identity and W.IsSkew (cj E) B d 0, all characters χX and χW and integer families mX and mW with IsHecke χX, IsHecke χW, ResEtaPow of χX with n, ResEtaPow of χW with d, HasExp B.emb χX mX and HasExp B.emb χW mW, and every subspace U of complex functions on UA E n and family lam of dominant weights with IsAutRepU U, HasWeightAt U (B.emb w).1 (lam w) for all w, and d + mW w ≤ 2 · (lam w).w k for all w and k, there exists a subspace U' of complex functions on UA E d with IsLift B χX χW mX mW lam U U'. IsLift says that U' satisfies IsAutRepU, that at every w there is a weight lam' with HasWeightAt U' (B.emb w).1 lam' and IsLiftWt (lam w) (mX w) (mW w) lam', and that for every v, t, τ, τ' the conditions CompAt U (splitPrime t) τ and CompAt U' (splitPrime t) τ' imply LocPair t χX χW τ τ'.

lines.name: UpperTheory.Gal.Int.Geo.geoOne_holds
lines.says: With no premises, the statement GeoOne holds. GeoOne takes a CM number field E with algebraic closure Ω, a prime l, a ring isomorphism ι from Qbar l to ℂ, an odd a, a natural number d with FieldOK E l d, an x in E with x² = −d, a finite set T of primes of E none of which satisfies IsSplitAt, two primes w₀ and v' of E that contain l, lie over different primes of the maximal real subfield and satisfy OneK x w₀ v', a finite set S of primes, and a space U of complex functions on UA E a satisfying AutOffT T U, TyEll E l a w₀ U, SphOffU w₀ S U, SatU U v' B for some B, and LacWtAt ι v' U. It concludes three things, namely that some size dd and homomorphism ρ from the automorphism group of Ω over E to GL_dd(Qbar l) satisfy VBase ι d U ρ, that at every prime w with UsPl d w, not containing l and with some SatU datum there is such a ρ that also satisfies ESAt ι ρ w (algSat a (normV w) B) for every B with SatU U w B, and that at every prime w containing l with OneK x w v', apart from w₀ and from v' and with some SatU datum, there is such a ρ with CrysAt ρ w and JumpsOcc U ι ρ w and there is such a ρ with PhiKilled ι ρ w a B for every B with SatU U w B.
lines.conclusion: GeoOne holds, a universally quantified statement whose own hypotheses and three-part conclusion are described in the entry of line 35, with each part asserting the existence of its own dd and ρ
lines.notation: ∀ E CM number field, ∀ Ω algebraic closure of E, ∀ l prime, ∀ ι ∈ (Qbar_l ≅ ℂ), ∀ a ∈ ℕ, Odd(a) ⇒ ∀ d ∈ ℕ, FieldOK(E, l, d) ⇒ ∀ x ∈ E, x² = −d ⇒ ∀ T finite set of primes of E, NonSplitSet(T) ⇒ ∀ w₀, v' primes of E, l ∈ w₀ ⇒ l ∈ v' ⇒ Apart(v', w₀) ⇒ OneK(x, w₀, v') ⇒ ∀ S finite set of primes, ∀ U ⊆ (UA(E, a) → ℂ), AutOffT(T, U) ⇒ TyEll(E, l, a, w₀, U) ⇒ SphOffU(w₀, S, U) ⇒ (∃ B, SatU(U, v', B)) ⇒ LacWtAt(ι, v', U) ⇒ [ (∃ dd, ρ, VBase(ι, d, U, ρ)) ∧ (∀ w, UsPl(d, w) ⇒ l ∉ w ⇒ (∃ B, SatU(U, w, B)) ⇒ ∃ dd, ρ, VBase(ι, d, U, ρ) ∧ ∀ B, SatU(U, w, B) ⇒ ESAt(ι, ρ, w, algSat(a, normV(w), B))) ∧ (∀ w, l ∈ w ⇒ OneK(x, w, v') ⇒ Apart(w, w₀) ⇒ Apart(w, v') ⇒ (∃ B, SatU(U, w, B)) ⇒ (∃ dd, ρ, VBase(ι, d, U, ρ) ∧ CrysAt(ρ, w) ∧ JumpsOcc(U, ι, ρ, w)) ∧ (∃ dd, ρ, VBase(ι, d, U, ρ) ∧ ∀ B, SatU(U, w, B) ⇒ PhiKilled(ι, ρ, w, a, B))) ]

terms.name: GeoOne
terms.gloss: The universally quantified statement written in the notation field.

terms.name: FieldOK
terms.gloss: The conjunction of ImQ E d, SqAt d l, evenness of the degree of the maximal real subfield over ℚ, and the requirement that every prime w of E not satisfying IsSplitAt does not contain l and is unramified over the ring of integers of the maximal real subfield, where ImQ, SqAt and IsSplitAt have no visible bodies.

terms.name: NonSplitSet
terms.gloss: The statement that no prime in T satisfies IsSplitAt.

terms.name: Apart
terms.gloss: The statement that two primes of E lie over different primes of the maximal real subfield.

terms.name: OneK
terms.gloss: The statement that an algebraic integer of E lying in the field ℚ(x) belongs to the prime w exactly when it belongs to the prime w'.

terms.name: AutOffT
terms.gloss: The statement that U satisfies IsAutRepU and satisfies IsUnramU at every prime that is not split and not in T.

terms.name: TyEll
terms.gloss: The statement that there exist m, an open compact torsion-free subgroup J of GL_a over the completion at w₀, a surjective homomorphism θ from J to the cyclic group ℤ/l^m, and a nontrivial character χ of that group, such that every SmIrr representation with a nonzero vector on which J acts through χ∘θ satisfies IsCuspidal, and such that U contains a nonzero function φ on which the elements x of locU a w₀ with cLoc w₀ x in J act through χ∘θ.

terms.name: SphOffU
terms.gloss: The statement that every prime w with IsSplitAt, apart from w₀ and satisfying ApartAll S w, has some B with SatU U w B.

terms.name: SatU
terms.gloss: The statement that some SmIrr representation σ of GL_a over the completion at w satisfies IsCompAlong with U and HasSatGL w σ.ρ B, both of which are names without visible bodies.

terms.name: LacWtAt
terms.gloss: The statement that some embedding τ of E into ℂ with OverPl ι τ v' and some weight lam satisfy HasWeightAt U τ lam and Lacunary (wtJumps lam), all resting on names without bodies.

terms.name: UsPl
terms.gloss: The statement that w satisfies IsSplitAt and that SqAt d q holds for every rational prime q contained in w.

terms.name: VBase
terms.gloss: The statement that ρ is continuous, satisfies IsSSRep, satisfies ESAt ι ρ w (algSat a (normV w) B) for every B with SatU U w B at all primes w outside some finite set with UsPl d w and l ∉ w, and satisfies HTRichEx ρ a, where IsSSRep and HTRichEx have no visible bodies.

terms.name: ESAt
terms.gloss: The statement that for every valuation ring A with IsPlaceOver A w, ρ is trivial on the subgroup Ine A, and for every σ with IsFrob A (normV w) σ the polynomial ∏ over b in B of (X − b), carried to Qbar l by the inverse of ι, vanishes at the matrix ρ(σ⁻¹).

terms.name: algSat
terms.gloss: The multiset obtained from B by multiplying each member by q^((n − 1)/2).

terms.name: normV
terms.gloss: The number of elements of the quotient of the ring of integers by the prime v.

terms.name: CrysAt
terms.gloss: The statement that for all auxiliary data P, AI, A, O, Bw satisfying LocTied, IsPlaceOver and Induces, the restriction of r to the subgroup Dec A satisfies IsCrysAt P Bw, a condition without visible body.

terms.name: JumpsOcc
terms.gloss: The statement that, for the same auxiliary data and each embedding τ, whenever U has weight lam at ι∘τ and J is the integer multiset equal to {(a − 1)/2 − z} over z in infOfWeight lam, there is a multiset J' with IsJumpsAt for ρ restricted to Dec A that contains every member of J.

terms.name: PhiKilled
terms.gloss: The statement that, for the same auxiliary data, ρ restricted to Dec A satisfies IsCrysAt and there is an element g of Weil h with deg g = −1 and a natural number m such that the polynomial charPol g of wdAt(…ρ…) divides the m-th power of the polynomial charPol g of satWD h a B.

terms.name: UA
terms.gloss: The subgroup UJ (conjAd E) 1 of the group GA E n, where UJ, conjAd and GA have no visible bodies.

lines.suggests: The names suggest a geometric construction of l-adic Galois representations attached to automorphic representations of a definite unitary group of odd rank over a CM field containing an imaginary quadratic field, with the Eichler–Shimura relation at good split primes, and crystallinity, Hodge–Tate jumps and control of the crystalline Frobenius at primes above l.
lines.why: The full quantifier structure and many middle-level definitions are visible, but the innermost conditions (IsSplitAt, ImQ, SqAt, HasSatGL, IsCompAlong, IsSSRep, HTRichEx, IsCrysAt, IsJumpsAt, IsFrob, Lacunary) are shown without bodies, and nineteen further definitions were left out of the dossier.

second.says: With no premises, the theorem states GeoOne, which quantifies over every CM number field E with algebraic closure Ω, every prime l, every ring isomorphism ι from Qbar l to ℂ, every odd a, every natural d with FieldOK E l d, every x in E with x² = −d, every finite set T of finite places none of which satisfies IsSplitAt, all finite places w₀ and v' that both contain l, lie over different primes of the maximal real subfield (Apart v' w₀) and satisfy OneK x w₀ v' (they contain the same integers of E lying in ℚ(x)), every finite set S of places and every subspace U of complex functions on UA E a with AutOffT T U, TyEll E l a w₀ U, SphOffU w₀ S U, some B with SatU U v' B, and LacWtAt ι v' U. Under these conditions three things hold together. First there exist a size dd and a homomorphism ρ from G E Ω to GL of size dd over Qbar l with VBase ι d U ρ, second for every place w with UsPl d w that does not contain l and has some B with SatU U w B there exist dd and ρ with VBase ι d U ρ such that ESAt ι ρ w (algSat a (normV w) B) holds for every B with SatU U w B, and third for every place w containing l with OneK x w v', Apart w w₀, Apart w v' and some B with SatU U w B there exist dd and ρ with VBase ι d U ρ, CrysAt ρ w and JumpsOcc U ι ρ w, and there also exist dd and ρ (possibly different) with VBase ι d U ρ such that PhiKilled ι ρ w a B holds for every B with SatU U w B.
second.conclusion: GeoOne holds, that is under the listed conditions on E, l, a, d, x, T, w₀, v', S and U there exist homomorphisms ρ with VBase, with ESAt at the places w satisfying UsPl away from l, and with CrysAt, JumpsOcc and PhiKilled at the listed places w above l
unclear: which of the two shown definitions named SatU the statement uses (both have the same body)

lines.name: UpperTheory.Gal.Int.Geo.geometric_realization_of_weight_one
lines.says: Assume the statement that the code calls HolomorphicLefschetzFormula, a fixed-point trace formula for pairs of finite étale maps between complex schemes. Then the statement GeoOne holds. GeoOne says that, for a CM number field E, a prime l, an odd number a and a complex space U of functions on a group UA E a meeting a list of conditions, there exist matrix representations ρ of the automorphism group of an algebraic closure of E over the field Qbar l that satisfy a condition called VBase, together with further conditions ESAt at certain primes not containing l and CrysAt, JumpsOcc and PhiKilled at certain primes containing l.
premises: HolomorphicLefschetzFormula holds, which reads as follows. For every scheme Z smooth of relative dimension d over Spec ℂ and satisfying IsProjOver, every scheme Y over Spec ℂ with two maps c1 and c2 from Y to Z over Spec ℂ that are both finite and étale, every finite set F of complex points of Y that consists exactly of the points y with y followed by c1 equal to y followed by c2, and every assignment A of d by d complex matrices such that each y in F satisfies IsTan with A y and det(1 − A y) ≠ 0, and for every natural number a, all the spaces hodgeH s a b are finite dimensional over ℂ and the sum over b from 0 to d of (−1)^b times the trace of hodgeTrace for c1 composed with hodgePull for c2 on hodgeH s a b equals the sum over y in F of the coefficient of X^a in det(1 + X·A y) divided by det(1 − A y)
lines.conclusion: GeoOne holds, which reads as follows. For all E, Ω, l, ι, odd a, d with FieldOK E l d, x in E with x² = −d, T with NonSplitSet T, primes w₀ and v' containing l with Apart v' w₀ and OneK x w₀ v', every finite set S of primes and every U with AutOffT T U, TyEll at w₀, SphOffU w₀ S U, some B with SatU U v' B, and LacWtAt ι v' U, three things hold. First, some dimension dd and some ρ satisfy VBase ι d U ρ. Second, for every prime w with UsPl d w, not containing l and having some B with SatU U w B, some dd and ρ satisfy VBase and ESAt ι ρ w (algSat a (normV w) B) for every B with SatU U w B. Third, for every prime w containing l with OneK x w v', Apart w w₀, Apart w v' and some B with SatU U w B, some dd and ρ satisfy VBase, CrysAt ρ w and JumpsOcc U ι ρ w, and some possibly different dd and ρ satisfy VBase and PhiKilled ι ρ w a B for every B with SatU U w B
lines.notation: HLF ⇒ GeoOne, where HLF is [∀ Z, s ∈ Hom(Z, Spec ℂ), d ∈ ℕ, s smooth of relative dimension d, IsProjOver(s) ⇒ ∀ Y, s' ∈ Hom(Y, Spec ℂ), c1, c2 ∈ Hom(Y, Z) with c1≫s = s', c2≫s = s', c1 and c2 finite étale ⇒ ∀ finite F ⊆ CxPts(s') with (∀ y, y ∈ F ⇔ y≫c1 = y≫c2), ∀ A from CxPts(s') to M_d(ℂ) with (∀ y ∈ F, IsTan(d, c1, c2, y, A y) ∧ det(1 − A y) ≠ 0), ∀ a ∈ ℕ, (∀ b, dim_ℂ hodgeH(s, a, b) < ∞) ∧ Σ_{b=0}^{d} (−1)^b tr(hodgeTrace_{c1}(a, b) ∘ hodgePull_{c2}(a, b)) = Σ_{y ∈ F} coeff_{X^a} det(1 + X·A y) / det(1 − A y)] and GeoOne is [∀ E CM number field, Ω algebraic closure of E, l prime, ι a ring isomorphism Qbar_l ≅ ℂ, a ∈ ℕ odd, d ∈ ℕ with FieldOK(E, l, d), x ∈ E with x² = −d, T finite set of primes of O_E with NonSplitSet(T), primes w₀, v' with l ∈ w₀, l ∈ v', Apart(v', w₀), OneK(x, w₀, v'), S finite set of primes, U a ℂ-subspace of the functions UA(E, a) → ℂ with AutOffT(T, U), TyEll(E, l, a, w₀, U), SphOffU(w₀, S, U), (∃ B, SatU(U, v', B)), LacWtAt(ι, v', U) ⇒ (∃ dd, ρ ∈ Hom(Aut_E(Ω), GL_dd(Qbar_l)), VBase(ι, d, U, ρ)) ∧ (∀ w, UsPl(d, w) ⇒ l ∉ w ⇒ (∃ B, SatU(U, w, B)) ⇒ ∃ dd, ρ, VBase(ι, d, U, ρ) ∧ ∀ B, SatU(U, w, B) ⇒ ESAt(ι, ρ, w, algSat(a, normV(w), B))) ∧ (∀ w, l ∈ w ⇒ OneK(x, w, v') ⇒ Apart(w, w₀) ⇒ Apart(w, v') ⇒ (∃ B, SatU(U, w, B)) ⇒ (∃ dd, ρ, VBase(ι, d, U, ρ) ∧ CrysAt(ρ, w) ∧ JumpsOcc(U, ι, ρ, w)) ∧ (∃ dd, ρ, VBase(ι, d, U, ρ) ∧ ∀ B, SatU(U, w, B) ⇒ PhiKilled(ι, ρ, w, a, B)))]

terms.name: HolomorphicLefschetzFormula
terms.gloss: The dossier shows its full body, the fixed-point trace identity written out in the premise, though the Hodge spaces and maps inside it rest on names that are not opened.

terms.name: GeoOne
terms.gloss: The dossier shows its full body, a universally quantified statement with a threefold conclusion about the existence of representations ρ.

terms.name: G E Ω
terms.gloss: This is the group of field automorphisms of Ω that fix E.

terms.name: Qbar l
terms.gloss: This is an abbreviation for a field that the code calls PadicAlgCl l, whose body is not shown.

terms.name: normV
terms.gloss: This is the number of elements of the quotient of the ring of integers by the prime ideal w.

terms.name: algSat
terms.gloss: Given n, q and a multiset B of nonzero complex numbers, this multiplies each member of B by the real power q^((n−1)/2).

terms.name: Apart
terms.gloss: Two primes of the ring of integers of E are Apart when the primes below them in the ring of integers of the maximal real subfield of E are different.

terms.name: OneK
terms.gloss: OneK x w w' says that every integer of E that lies in the subfield ℚ(x) belongs to w exactly when it belongs to w'.

terms.name: NonSplitSet
terms.gloss: This says that no prime in T satisfies the condition that the code calls IsSplitAt, which is shown without a body.

terms.name: FieldOK
terms.gloss: This is the conjunction of ImQ E d, SqAt d l, evenness of the degree over ℚ of the maximal real subfield of E, and the requirement that every prime w not satisfying IsSplitAt does not contain l and satisfies Mathlib's unramifiedness predicate over the integers of the maximal real subfield, where ImQ, SqAt and IsSplitAt are shown without bodies.

terms.name: UsPl
terms.gloss: UsPl d w says that IsSplitAt w holds and that SqAt d q holds for every rational prime q lying in w, with both inner names shown without bodies.

terms.name: UA E a
terms.gloss: This is a subgroup of a group GA E a, given as UJ (conjAd E) 1, and none of those names is opened.

terms.name: AutOffT
terms.gloss: This says that IsAutRepU U holds and that IsUnramU U w holds for every prime w outside T that does not satisfy IsSplitAt, with those three names shown without bodies.

terms.name: TyEll
terms.gloss: This asks for an exponent m, an open compact torsion-free subgroup J of GL_a over the completion of E at w₀, a surjective homomorphism θ from J to ℤ/l^m, and a nontrivial character χ of ℤ/l^m such that every SmIrr object having a nonzero vector on which J acts through χ∘θ satisfies IsCuspidal, and such that U contains a nonzero φ on which the elements of locU a w₀ that cLoc sends into J act through RU by χ∘θ, where SmIrr, IsCuspidal, locU, cLoc and RU are not opened.

terms.name: SatU
terms.gloss: SatU U w B says that some SmIrr object σ for GL_a over the completion of E at w satisfies IsCompAlong with U and HasSatGL with B, and those names are shown without bodies. The dossier lists two definitions of this name with the same body.

terms.name: SphOffU
terms.gloss: This says that every prime w with IsSplitAt w, Apart w w₀ and ApartAll S w has some B with SatU U w B, where ApartAll is not shown.

terms.name: LacWtAt
terms.gloss: This says that some embedding τ of E into ℂ satisfies OverPl ι τ v' and some lam of type DomWeight a satisfies HasWeightAt U τ lam and Lacunary (wtJumps lam), and none of those names is opened.

terms.name: VBase
terms.gloss: VBase ι d U ρ says that ρ is continuous, that IsSSRep ρ holds, that outside some finite set of primes every prime w with UsPl d w and l ∉ w satisfies ESAt ι ρ w (algSat a (normV w) B) for every B with SatU U w B, and that HTRichEx ρ a holds, where IsSSRep and HTRichEx are not shown.

terms.name: ESAt
terms.gloss: ESAt ι ρ w B says that for every valuation subring A of Ω with IsPlaceOver A w, ρ is trivial on the set Ine A and, for every σ with IsFrob A (normV w) σ, the matrix ρ(σ⁻¹) is a root of the polynomial ∏ (X − b) over b in B carried to Qbar l by the inverse of ι, where IsPlaceOver, Ine and IsFrob are not shown.

terms.name: CrysAt
terms.gloss: This says that for every choice of local data of the types LocPrime, LocAinf, LocTied and LocBridge with Induces, and every valuation subring A with IsPlaceOver A w, the restriction of the representation to the subgroup Dec A satisfies IsCrysAt, and none of those names is opened.

terms.name: JumpsOcc
terms.gloss: This says that, for the same kind of local data and every embedding τ and every lam with HasWeightAt U (ι∘τ) lam, any multiset J of integers that equals the image of infOfWeight lam under z ↦ (a−1)/2 − z is contained in some multiset J' with IsJumpsAt for ρ restricted to Dec A, and the inner names are not opened.

terms.name: PhiKilled
terms.gloss: This says that, for the same kind of local data, ρ restricted to Dec A satisfies IsCrysAt and there are an element g of Weil h with deg g = −1 and a natural number m such that the polynomial charPol at g of the object wdAt built from ρ divides the m-th power of charPol at g of the object satWD h a B, and the inner names are not opened.

terms.name: IsProjOver
terms.gloss: This says that the map factors as a closed immersion into PSpace R N for some N followed by the structure map of PSpace R N, where PSpace is not shown.

terms.name: CxPts
terms.gloss: This is the type PtsOver p (spMap σ), whose two inner names are shown without bodies.

terms.name: IsTan
terms.gloss: IsTan says that there are affine open sets U in Z and V in Y, with V inside the preimages of U under c1 and c2 and with y in V, d sections t on U, and a ℂ-linear map φ from the Kähler differentials of the sections on V to ℂ^d that is semilinear for evaluation at y, sends the differential of the c1-pullback of t_l to the l-th basis vector, sends the differential of the c2-pullback of t_j to row j of A, and vanishes only on sums of differentials with coefficients vanishing at y.

terms.name: hodgeH, hodgePull, hodgeTrace
terms.gloss: hodgeH s j q is coh (Omega s j) q, and hodgePull and hodgeTrace are linear maps between such spaces in opposite directions built from cohOn.pull, omegaPull, cohOn.map and omegaTrace, none of which is opened.

lines.suggests: The names suggest that the hypothesis is the holomorphic Lefschetz fixed-point formula for a correspondence on a smooth projective complex variety acting on Hodge cohomology, and that the conclusion is the construction, in the cohomology of unitary Shimura varieties, of l-adic Galois representations attached to automorphic representations of a unitary group, with local-global compatibility at unramified split places, crystallinity, Hodge–Tate weights and a Frobenius eigenvalue relation at places above l.
lines.why: The full logical shape of both the hypothesis and GeoOne is shown, but most leaf conditions rest on names without bodies and 61 definitions were left out of the dossier.

second.says: The theorem claims that if the condition HolomorphicLefschetzFormula holds, then the statement GeoOne holds. HolomorphicLefschetzFormula says that for every scheme Z smooth of relative dimension d and projective over Spec ℂ, every scheme Y over Spec ℂ with two finite etale maps c1 and c2 to Z over Spec ℂ, every finite set F of complex points of Y that is exactly the set of points y with y followed by c1 equal to y followed by c2, and every assignment A of d by d complex matrices such that for each y in F the condition IsTan holds for A y and det(1 − A y) is not 0, for every natural a all the spaces hodgeH s a b are finite dimensional over ℂ and the sum over b in range (d+1) of (−1)^b times the trace of hodgeTrace h1 a b composed with hodgePull h2 a b equals the sum over y in F of the coefficient of X^a in det(1 + X·A y) divided by det(1 − A y). GeoOne says that for every CM number field E with algebraic closure Ω, prime l, ring isomorphism ι from Qbar l to ℂ, odd natural a, natural d with FieldOK E l d, x in E with x^2 = −d, finite set T of primes with NonSplitSet T, primes w₀ and v' both containing l with Apart v' w₀ and OneK x w₀ v', finite set S of primes and complex subspace U of functions on UA E a satisfying AutOffT T U, TyEll E l a w₀ U, SphOffU w₀ S U, existence of B with SatU U v' B, and LacWtAt ι v' U, three things hold together, namely (1) there exist dd and a homomorphism ρ from G E Ω to GL of size dd over Qbar l with VBase ι d U ρ, (2) for every prime w with UsPl d w, l not in w and some B with SatU U w B there exist dd and ρ with VBase ι d U ρ such that every B with SatU U w B gives ESAt ι ρ w (algSat a (normV w) B), and (3) for every prime w containing l with OneK x w v', Apart w w₀, Apart w v' and some B with SatU U w B there exist dd and ρ with VBase ι d U ρ, CrysAt ρ w and JumpsOcc U ι ρ w, and there also exist dd and ρ (possibly different) with VBase ι d U ρ such that every B with SatU U w B gives PhiKilled ι ρ w a B.
premises: hW, the condition HolomorphicLefschetzFormula holds (a universally quantified trace identity for pairs of finite etale maps between schemes over Spec ℂ, with fixed-point set F and matrices A y satisfying IsTan and det(1 − A y) ≠ 0)
second.conclusion: GeoOne holds, that is, under its listed hypotheses on E, Ω, l, ι, odd a, d, x, T, w₀, v', S and U, the three-part conjunction about existence of dd and ρ with VBase, with ESAt at primes w satisfying UsPl and not containing l, and with CrysAt, JumpsOcc and PhiKilled at primes w containing l
unclear: SatU (two definitions with the same body are shown, in CongL and in TP.Sub, and the dossier does not say which one GeoOne uses)
Datum, HTGroup, Link, GBase and k (listed as variables in scope for HolomorphicLefschetzFormula but not appearing in its body, and the body of Datum is cut)

lines.name: UpperTheory.Gal.Int.Geo.steps_holds
lines.says: The theorem states, with no hypothesis, that a bundle of seventeen propositions that the code calls Steps holds. Most of the seventeen are universally quantified implications about homomorphisms ρ from the group G E Ω, for a number field E with an algebraic closure Ω, into invertible matrices over the field Qbar l, about objects H of a type HTower E with a function θ on H.Γ, or about general matrix representations of a group. One of them, CharEx, instead asserts the existence of a map L that sends pairs (χ, n) to homomorphisms from G E Ω to the units of Qbar l, and another, SatCard, concerns a function space U and a multiset B and no representation. Nearly all the conditions that these implications relate are names whose bodies this dossier does not show.
lines.conclusion: all seventeen fields of Steps hold, namely RepEx, ESStep, CrysStep, JumpStep, PhiStep, CutStep, TwES, TwCrys, TwJ, TwPhi, PhiOf, SatCard, JumpsOf, RichOf, CharEx, SSLeft and ContLeft
lines.notation: Steps = RepEx ∧ ESStep ∧ CrysStep ∧ JumpStep ∧ PhiStep ∧ CutStep ∧ TwES ∧ TwCrys ∧ TwJ ∧ TwPhi ∧ PhiOf ∧ SatCard ∧ JumpsOf ∧ RichOf ∧ CharEx ∧ SSLeft ∧ ContLeft. Throughout, E is a number field, Ω an algebraic closure of E, l a prime, ι a ring isomorphism Qbar_l ≅ ℂ, H ∈ HTower(E), θ a function H.Γ → Qbar_l, ρ ∈ Hom(G(E, Ω), GL_dd(Qbar_l)), w a prime of O_E. RepEx is [Nice(H) ⇒ ∃ dd, ρ, ρ continuous ∧ IsSSRep(ρ) ∧ IsPiece(H, θ, ρ)]. ESStep is [Nice(H), ρ continuous, IsPiece(H, θ, ρ), l ∉ w, CongAt(H, θ, w, n, ϑ), HasRoots(ι, w, n, ϑ, R) ⇒ ESAt(ι, ρ, w, R)]. CrysStep is [Nice(H), ρ continuous, IsPiece(H, θ, ρ), l ∈ w, C ∈ Cover(H, θ, Ow(w)), C.Onto ⇒ CrysAt(ρ, w)]. JumpStep is [Nice(H), ρ continuous, IsPiece(H, θ, ρ), l ∈ w, GoodAt(H, θ, w) ⇒ JOcc(ι, ρ, w, HodgeAt(ι, H, θ))]. PhiStep is [Nice(H), ρ continuous, IsPiece(H, θ, ρ), l ∈ w, CongAt(H, θ, w, n, ϑ), HasRoots(ι, w, n, ϑ, R) ⇒ PhiK(ι, ρ, w, R)]. CutStep is [for any field L and θ with values in L, Nice(H) ⇒ ∀ w, (GoodAtW(H, θ, w) ⇒ GoodAt(H, θ, w)) ∧ ∀ n, ϑ, CongAtW(H, θ, w, n, ϑ) ⇒ CongAt(H, θ, w, n, ϑ)]. With χ ∈ Hom(G(E, Ω), Qbar_l^×), ρ and χ continuous, c ∈ ℂ, m a function from embeddings E → ℂ to ℤ, and Cl(ι, rk1 χ, w, {c}, τ ↦ {m(ι∘τ)}) assumed, TwES is [l ∉ w, ESAt(ι, ρ, w, R) ⇒ ESAt(ι, tw(ρ, χ), w, R·c)], TwCrys is [CrysAt(ρ, w) ⇒ CrysAt(tw(ρ, χ), w)], TwJ is [∀ Q, JOcc(ι, ρ, w, Q) ⇒ JOcc(ι, tw(ρ, χ), w, (τ, j) ↦ Q(τ, j − m τ))], TwPhi is [PhiK(ι, ρ, w, R) ⇒ PhiK(ι, tw(ρ, χ), w, R·c)]. PhiOf is [|B| = a, PhiK(ι, ρ, w, algSat(a, normV(w), B)) ⇒ PhiKilled(ι, ρ, w, a, B)]. SatCard is [E CM, SatU(U, w, B) ⇒ |B| = a]. JumpsOf is [E CM, (∀ τ, OverPl(ι, τ, w) ⇒ ∀ lam, HasWeightAt(U, τ, lam) ⇒ ∀ j ∈ wtJumps(lam), Q(τ, j)), JOcc(ι, ρ, w, Q) ⇒ JumpsOcc(U, ι, ρ, w)]. RichOf is [E CM, l ∈ v, LacWtAt(ι, v, U), JumpsOcc(U, ι, ρ, v) ⇒ HTRichEx(ρ, a)]. CharEx is [∀ E, Ω, l, ι, ∃ L sending (χ ∈ HChar(E), n) to a homomorphism G(E, Ω) → Qbar_l^×, (∀ χ, n, IsAlgPos(χ, n) ⇒ L(χ, n) continuous ∧ ∀ w, χ.UnrAt(w) ⇒ Cl(ι, rk1(L(χ, n)), w, {χ.val(w)}, τ ↦ {−n(ι∘τ)})) ∧ (∀ χ, n, χ', n', IsAlgPos(χ, n) ⇒ IsAlgPos(χ', n') ⇒ L(χ, n) = L(χ', n') ⇒ χ = χ')]. SSLeft is [∀ group Γ, field k, a, b, (∀ r, s, IsSSRep(sumRep(r, s)) ⇒ IsSSRep(r)) ∧ (∀ r, r', RepIso(r, r') ⇒ IsSSRep(r) ⇒ IsSSRep(r')) ∧ (∀ r, c, IsSSRep(r) ⇒ IsSSRep(tw(r, c)))]. ContLeft is [∀ topological group Γ, field k with a topological ring structure, a, b, (∀ r, s, sumRep(r, s) continuous ⇒ r continuous) ∧ (∀ r, r', RepIso(r, r') ⇒ r continuous ⇒ r' continuous) ∧ (∀ r, c, r continuous ⇒ c continuous ⇒ tw(r, c) continuous) ∧ (∀ c, c continuous ⇒ rk1(c) continuous)]

terms.name: Steps
terms.gloss: This is a structure whose seventeen fields are the propositions RepEx, ESStep, CrysStep, JumpStep, PhiStep, CutStep, TwES, TwCrys, TwJ, TwPhi, PhiOf, SatCard, JumpsOf, RichOf, CharEx, SSLeft and ContLeft, so it is their conjunction.

terms.name: RepEx
terms.gloss: For every H with Nice H and every θ there exist a dimension dd and a continuous ρ with IsSSRep ρ and IsPiece H θ ρ.

terms.name: ESStep
terms.gloss: For Nice H, continuous ρ with IsPiece H θ ρ, and a prime w not containing l, the conditions CongAt H θ w n ϑ and HasRoots ι w n ϑ R imply ESAt ι ρ w R.

terms.name: CrysStep
terms.gloss: For Nice H, continuous ρ with IsPiece H θ ρ, and a prime w containing l, the existence of an object C of type Cover H θ (Ow w) with C.Onto implies CrysAt ρ w.

terms.name: JumpStep
terms.gloss: For Nice H, continuous ρ with IsPiece H θ ρ, and a prime w containing l, the condition GoodAt H θ w implies JOcc ι ρ w taken with the predicate HodgeAt ι H θ.

terms.name: PhiStep
terms.gloss: For Nice H, continuous ρ with IsPiece H θ ρ, and a prime w containing l, the conditions CongAt H θ w n ϑ and HasRoots ι w n ϑ R imply PhiK ι ρ w R.

terms.name: CutStep
terms.gloss: For Nice H and every prime w, GoodAtW implies GoodAt and CongAtW implies CongAt, for θ with values in any field L.

terms.name: TwES, TwCrys, TwJ, TwPhi
terms.gloss: Given continuous ρ and a continuous character χ with Cl ι (rk1 χ) w {c} (τ ↦ {m(ι∘τ)}), these say that ESAt and PhiK pass from ρ to tw ρ χ with the multiset multiplied by c, that CrysAt passes from ρ to tw ρ χ, and that JOcc passes with the predicate shifted by m τ, where TwES also needs l ∉ w.

terms.name: PhiOf
terms.gloss: If B has exactly a members and PhiK ι ρ w (algSat a (normV w) B) holds then PhiKilled ι ρ w a B holds.

terms.name: SatCard
terms.gloss: For a CM number field E, SatU U w B implies that the multiset B has exactly a members.

terms.name: JumpsOf
terms.gloss: If a predicate Q holds at (τ, j) for every τ with OverPl ι τ w, every lam with HasWeightAt U τ lam and every j in wtJumps lam, and JOcc ι ρ w Q holds, then JumpsOcc U ι ρ w holds.

terms.name: RichOf
terms.gloss: For a prime v containing l, LacWtAt ι v U and JumpsOcc U ι ρ v together imply HTRichEx ρ a.

terms.name: CharEx
terms.gloss: There is an assignment L from pairs (χ, n) to homomorphisms from G E Ω to the units of Qbar l such that, when IsAlgPos χ n holds, L χ n is continuous and satisfies Cl at every w with χ.UnrAt w with the data {χ.val w} and τ ↦ {−n(ι∘τ)}, and such that L χ n = L χ' n' forces χ = χ' when both pairs satisfy IsAlgPos.

terms.name: SSLeft
terms.gloss: For any group and field, IsSSRep passes from sumRep r s to r, across RepIso, and from r to tw r c.

terms.name: ContLeft
terms.gloss: For a topological group and a field with a topological ring structure, continuity passes from sumRep r s to r, across RepIso, to tw r c from continuous r and c, and from c to rk1 c.

terms.name: HTower, Nice, IsPiece, Cover, Ow, GoodAt, GoodAtW, CongAt, CongAtW, HasRoots, HodgeAt, JOcc, PhiK
terms.gloss: These types and conditions are shown with their signatures only, so the dossier does not say what they are.

terms.name: ESAt, CrysAt, JumpsOcc, PhiKilled, SatU, OverPl, HasWeightAt, wtJumps, LacWtAt, HTRichEx, IsSSRep
terms.gloss: These conditions on a representation, a prime or a function space are shown in this dossier without bodies or not at all.

terms.name: tw, rk1, sumRep, RepIso, Cl, HChar, IsAlgPos
terms.gloss: These operations and conditions on representations and characters are among the definitions left out of the dossier.

terms.name: G E Ω, Qbar l, normV, algSat, UA
terms.gloss: These are shown in this dossier with signatures only, as a group attached to E and Ω, a field attached to l, a natural number attached to a prime, a multiset of complex numbers, and a subgroup of GA E n.

lines.suggests: The names suggest a checklist of the steps of a construction of Galois representations from the cohomology of a tower of varieties with Hecke eigenvalues θ, covering existence of a semisimple piece, the Eichler–Shimura congruence relation away from l, crystallinity, Hodge–Tate jumps and a Frobenius relation at l, compatibility of each property with twisting by a character, Galois characters attached to algebraic Hecke characters, and the stability of semisimplicity and continuity under direct summands, isomorphism and twists. The name G E Ω suggests the automorphism group of Ω over E, which is the absolute Galois group of E.
lines.why: The conjunction and the quantifier shape of every field are visible, but almost every condition named inside the fields is shown without a body, so the mathematical content cannot be read off.

second.says: The theorem claims, with no hypothesis, that the structure Steps holds, which is the conjunction of seventeen conditions named rep (RepEx), es (ESStep), crys (CrysStep), jump (JumpStep), phi (PhiStep), cut (CutStep), twES (TwES), twCrys (TwCrys), twJ (TwJ), twPhi (TwPhi), phiOf (PhiOf), card (SatCard), jumpsOf (JumpsOf), rich (RichOf), char (TP.Sub.CharEx), ss (TP.Sub.SSLeft) and cont (TP.Sub.ContLeft). For every number field E with algebraic closure Ω, prime l, HTower H over E with Nice H and θ from H.Γ to Qbar l, RepEx gives some dd and a continuous ρ from G E Ω to GL of size dd over Qbar l with IsSSRep ρ and IsPiece H θ ρ, and for any continuous ρ with IsPiece H θ ρ and prime w, ESStep gives ESAt ι ρ w R when l is not in w and CongAt H θ w n ϑ and HasRoots ι w n ϑ R hold, CrysStep gives CrysAt ρ w when l is in w and some Cover of H θ over Ow w is Onto, JumpStep gives JOcc ι ρ w (HodgeAt ι H θ) when l is in w and GoodAt H θ w, PhiStep gives PhiK ι ρ w R when l is in w with CongAt and HasRoots, and CutStep says GoodAtW implies GoodAt and CongAtW implies CongAt. For continuous ρ and continuous character χ with Cl ι (rk1 χ) w {c} (τ ↦ {m(ι∘τ)}), the four twist conditions say that ESAt with R at w not containing l passes to tw ρ χ with R multiplied by c, CrysAt passes to tw ρ χ, JOcc with Q passes to tw ρ χ with Q τ (j − m τ), and PhiK with R passes to tw ρ χ with R multiplied by c, while PhiOf says B.card = a and PhiK ι ρ w (algSat a (normV w) B) give PhiKilled ι ρ w a B, SatCard says SatU U w B gives B.card = a, JumpsOf says that if Q τ j holds for every τ with OverPl ι τ w, every lam with HasWeightAt U τ lam and every j in wtJumps lam, then JOcc ι ρ w Q gives JumpsOcc U ι ρ w, RichOf says l in v, LacWtAt ι v U and JumpsOcc U ι ρ v give HTRichEx ρ a, CharEx says there is a map L from pairs (χ, n) to characters of G E Ω that for IsAlgPos χ n is continuous, satisfies Cl ι (rk1 (L χ n)) w {χ.val w} (τ ↦ {−n(ι∘τ)}) at every w with χ.UnrAt w, and has L χ n = L χ' n' implying χ = χ', SSLeft says IsSSRep passes from sumRep r s to r, along RepIso and to tw r c, and ContLeft says continuity passes from sumRep r s to r, along RepIso, to tw r c for continuous c, and from c to rk1 c.
second.conclusion: Steps holds, meaning all seventeen of its component conditions hold
unclear: PhiK (two definitions of this name are listed, one in Int.Geo and one in CuspRep, both without body)

first_errors: A says that "each of the seventeen is a universally quantified implication" about representations ρ, towers H or general matrix representations, but the Lean text of CharEx is "∀ … (ι : Qbar l ≃+* ℂ), ∃ L : HChar E → ((E →+* ℂ) → ℤ) → (G E Ω →* (Qbar l)ˣ)" followed by a conjunction, which is an existence statement about a map L to characters, and SatCard reads "SatU U w B → B.card = a" and concerns U and B and no representation.

A calls G E Ω "the automorphism group of an algebraic closure of a number field E" and writes "Aut_E(Ω)" in the notation, but this dossier shows only "abbrev G (F Ω : Type*) [Field F] [Field Ω] [Algebra F Ω]" without a body, so the meaning of G is asserted outside the field suggests.
second_errors: B places CutStep under the data "θ from H.Γ to Qbar l" and says only that "GoodAtW implies GoodAt and CongAtW implies CongAt", but the Lean text has "(L : Type) [Field L] (H : HTower E) (θ : H.Γ → L)", so the universal quantifier over every field L is lost.

B says that L "has L χ n = L χ' n' implying χ = χ'" with at most IsAlgPos χ n assumed, but the Lean text reads "IsAlgPos χ n → IsAlgPos χ' n' → L χ n = L χ' n' → χ = χ'", so the premise IsAlgPos χ' n' is missing.

lines.name: UpperTheory.Gal.Int.Geo.kodaira_spencer_of_weight_one
lines.says: Assume the statement that the code calls HolomorphicLefschetzFormula, a fixed-point trace formula for pairs of finite étale maps between complex schemes. Then a bundle of six propositions that the code calls KSAll holds. The six say that a base object gb with IsStd exists when D.a = 1, that the type KS L gb k is never empty when Sc D G holds, and that the tower T.tower N g obtained from any member T of KS satisfies the conditions Nice, GoodAtW and CongAtW under stated hypotheses, and that the object bcAlong (T.tower N g) τ, for a ring map τ from R to ℂ, satisfies HOcc under stated hypotheses.
premises: HolomorphicLefschetzFormula holds, which reads as follows. For every scheme Z smooth of relative dimension d over Spec ℂ and satisfying IsProjOver, every scheme Y over Spec ℂ with two maps c1 and c2 from Y to Z over Spec ℂ that are both finite and étale, every finite set F of complex points of Y that consists exactly of the points y with y followed by c1 equal to y followed by c2, and every assignment A of d by d complex matrices such that each y in F satisfies IsTan with A y and det(1 − A y) ≠ 0, and for every natural number a, all the spaces hodgeH s a b are finite dimensional over ℂ and the sum over b from 0 to d of (−1)^b times the trace of hodgeTrace for c1 composed with hodgePull for c2 on hodgeH s a b equals the sum over y in F of the coefficient of X^a in det(1 + X·A y) divided by det(1 − A y)
lines.conclusion: all six fields of KSAll hold, namely StdEx, KSEx, KSNice, KSGood, KSCong and KSHodge
lines.notation: HLF ⇒ StdEx ∧ KSEx ∧ KSNice ∧ KSGood ∧ KSCong ∧ KSHodge, with HLF as in line 36. Throughout, p is a prime, D ∈ Datum(p), G ∈ HTGroup(p), L ∈ Link(D, G). StdEx is [∀ p, D with D.a = 1, ∀ number field E, ring isomorphism e from D.F to E, ∃ gb ∈ GBase(D.toG, E), IsStd(e, gb)]. KSEx is [∀ p, D, G, L, Sc(D, G) ⇒ ∀ field R that is a ℚ-algebra, gb ∈ GBase(D.toG, R), k ∈ ℕ, KS(L, gb, k) ≠ ∅]. KSNice is [Sc(D, G) ⇒ ∀ R, gb, k, T ∈ KS(L, gb, k), N ∈ Lv(p), index type J, g from J to Mem(L, N), Nice(T.tower(N, g))]. KSGood is [Sc(D, G) ⇒ ∀ number field E, e from D.F to E, gb ∈ GBase(D.toG, E), IsStd(e, gb) ⇒ ∀ k, T ∈ KS(L, gb, k), N, J, field A, g from J to Mem(L, N), θ from J to A, prime w of O_E, ideal 𝔴 of O_{D.F}, IsPl(e, w, 𝔴) ⇒ GoodGrp(g, θ, 𝔴) ⇒ GoodAtW(T.tower(N, g), θ, w)]. KSCong is [same data and IsPl(e, w, 𝔴) ⇒ ∀ ϑ from ℕ to A, CongGrp(g, θ, 𝔴, ϑ) ⇒ CongAtW(T.tower(N, g), θ, w, D.n, ϑ)]. KSHodge is [Sc(D, G) ⇒ ∀ lam assigning to each embedding τ of D.F in ℂ a non-increasing function Fin(G.n) → ℕ, ∃ k ∈ ℕ, ∀ field R over ℚ, gb ∈ GBase(D.toG, R), T ∈ KS(L, gb, k), N, J, g from J to Mem(L, N), θ from J to ℂ, f from G.GAf to ℂ, IsFnL(L, N.1, f) ⇒ Spec(L, lam, L.KN(N.1), j ↦ (g j).fn, θ, f) ⇒ ∀ ring map τ from R to ℂ with τ(gb.ρ) = D.ρc and (∀ i, c, τ(gb.t_i(c)) = D.tau_i(c)), ∀ ring automorphism σ of ℂ, i₀ ∈ Fin(D.a), h from Fin(G.n) to ℕ, IsHExp(D.tau_{i₀}, epsOf(D), conjWt(σ, lam), h) ⇒ ∀ i, HOcc(bcAlong(T.tower(N, g), τ), j ↦ σ(θ j), h i)]

terms.name: KSAll
terms.gloss: This is a structure whose six fields are the propositions StdEx, KSEx, KSNice, KSGood, KSCong and KSHodge, so it is their conjunction.

terms.name: HolomorphicLefschetzFormula
terms.gloss: The dossier shows its full body, the fixed-point trace identity written out in the premise, though the Hodge spaces and maps inside it rest on names that are not opened.

terms.name: StdEx
terms.gloss: For every D with D.a = 1 and every number field E with a ring isomorphism e from D.F, some gb of type GBase D.toG E satisfies IsStd e gb.

terms.name: KSEx
terms.gloss: When Sc D G holds, the type KS L gb k has a member for every field R over ℚ, every gb over R and every natural number k.

terms.name: KSNice
terms.gloss: When Sc D G holds, the tower T.tower N g of every member T of KS L gb k, every level N and every family g satisfies Nice.

terms.name: KSGood
terms.gloss: When Sc D G, IsStd e gb and IsPl e w 𝔴 hold, GoodGrp g θ 𝔴 implies GoodAtW for the tower T.tower N g, the function θ and the prime w.

terms.name: KSCong
terms.gloss: When Sc D G, IsStd e gb and IsPl e w 𝔴 hold, CongGrp g θ 𝔴 ϑ implies CongAtW for the tower T.tower N g, θ, w, the number D.n and ϑ.

terms.name: KSHodge
terms.gloss: When Sc D G holds, for each family lam of non-increasing weights there is a k such that, for every T in KS L gb k and data with IsFnL and Spec, every ring map τ from R to ℂ matching gb with D, every ring automorphism σ of ℂ and every h with IsHExp, the object bcAlong (T.tower N g) τ satisfies HOcc with the function σ∘θ and each value h i.

terms.name: Datum p
terms.gloss: This is a structure holding a CM number field F with its conjugation on integers, an integer ω of F with integer trace tr and norm nm of negative discriminant prime to p and with x² − tr·x + nm having a root modulo p, a ring O over the integers of F that is free of rank m²·[F:ℚ] over ℤ with an involution and a matrix splitting at p, a free ℤ-module La of rank m·n·[F:ℚ] with an alternating form, a number a, a complex root ρc and a embeddings tau of F in ℂ sending ω to ρc, and a complex structure condition whose text is cut off in the dossier.

terms.name: HTGroup p
terms.gloss: This is a structure holding a CM number field F with a quadratic subfield Kq having no real embedding and a map of Kq to ℚ_p, a central simple F-algebra C of dimension n² with an involution extending complex conjugation, matrix realisations and Hermitian Gram matrices at each infinite place of signature (1, n−1) or (0, n), a list of m embeddings of F in PadicAlgCl p over the map u, and embeddings of an algebraic closure of ℚ in PadicAlgCl p and in ℂ.

terms.name: Link D G
terms.gloss: This is a structure holding a ring isomorphism from D.F to G.F, the equality G.n = D.n, an injective representation of G.C on a rational space VQ D whose image is the commutant of the action of D.O, and compatibilities between the embeddings, signatures and forms of D and G.

terms.name: GBase
terms.gloss: A GBase over a ring R is an element ρ of R with ρ² − tr·ρ + nm = 0 together with ring maps t_i from the integers of the field to R, one for each i below a, that all send ω to ρ and are pairwise comaximal in the sense that the differences t_i(x) − t_j(x) generate the unit ideal.

terms.name: Sc, IsStd, IsPl, KS, Lv, Mem, GoodGrp, CongGrp
terms.gloss: These are shown with signatures only, as a condition on D and G, a condition on e and gb, a condition relating w and 𝔴 through e, a type of objects attached to L, gb and k, a type of levels, a type of objects at a level, and two conditions on g and θ at 𝔴.

terms.name: Nice, GoodAtW, CongAtW, HOcc, bcAlong
terms.gloss: These are shown with signatures only, as conditions on an object of type HTower and an operation that takes an object of type HTower k and a ring map τ from k to a field K and returns an object of type HTower K.

terms.name: IsFnL, Spec, IsHExp, conjWt, epsOf
terms.gloss: These are shown with signatures only, as conditions on functions on G.GAf and on weights, and two functions that produce weights and natural numbers.

terms.name: D.toG, T.tower, L.KN, G.GAf, (g j).fn
terms.gloss: These projections and constructions are used in the statements but their definitions do not appear in the dossier.

terms.name: IsProjOver, CxPts, IsTan, hodgeH, hodgePull, hodgeTrace
terms.gloss: These are the ingredients of the hypothesis, shown with bodies that describe a closed immersion into PSpace, points over Spec ℂ, a tangent-matrix condition at a point through Kähler differentials, and cohomology spaces of Omega with pullback and trace maps, resting on names that are not opened.

lines.suggests: The names suggest that KS stands for a Kodaira–Spencer type package attaching to PEL data of unitary type with one distinguished embedding a tower of varieties with automorphic sheaves of weight k, and that the six fields say this package exists, is well behaved, has good reduction and a congruence relation at suitable primes, and has the Hodge numbers predicted by the weight lam, the last being where the Lefschetz formula is used. The name bcAlong suggests the base change of a tower along the ring map τ, so that the last field concerns the tower after base change to ℂ.
lines.why: The hypothesis and the quantifier shape of all six fields are shown in full, but the central objects KS, Sc, IsStd, Nice, GoodAtW, CongAtW and HOcc are shown without bodies and 24 definitions were left out.

second.says: The theorem claims that if the condition HolomorphicLefschetzFormula holds (the same trace identity for pairs of finite etale maps between schemes over Spec ℂ as in line 36), then the structure KSAll holds, which is the conjunction of six conditions named std (StdEx), ex (KSEx), nice (KSNice), good (KSGood), cong (KSCong) and hodge (KSHodge). StdEx says that for every prime p, every Datum D with D.a = 1, every number field E and ring isomorphism e from D.F to E there is a gb in GBase D.toG E with IsStd e gb, KSEx says that for every p, D, HTGroup G and Link L with Sc D G, every field R that is a ℚ-algebra, every gb in GBase D.toG R and every natural k the type KS L gb k is nonempty, KSNice says that under the same data every T in KS L gb k, every N in Lv p, every type J and every g from J to Mem L N give Nice (T.tower N g), and KSGood and KSCong say that for Sc D G, a number field E with e and gb satisfying IsStd e gb, any k, T, N, J, field A, g, θ from J to A, prime w of E and ideal 𝔴 of the integers of D.F with IsPl e w 𝔴, the condition GoodGrp g θ 𝔴 gives GoodAtW (T.tower N g) θ w and, for every ϑ from ℕ to A, the condition CongGrp g θ 𝔴 ϑ gives CongAtW (T.tower N g) θ w D.n ϑ. KSHodge says that for Sc D G and every lam from embeddings of D.F in ℂ to functions Fin G.n → ℕ with each lam τ antitone there exists a natural k such that for every field R over ℚ, gb, T in KS L gb k, N, J, g, θ from J to ℂ and f from G.GAf to ℂ with IsFnL L N.1 f and Spec L lam (L.KN N.1) (j ↦ (g j).fn) θ f, every ring map τ from R to ℂ with τ gb.ρ = D.ρc and τ (gb.t i c) = D.tau i c for all i and c, every ring automorphism σ of ℂ, every i₀ in Fin D.a and every h from Fin G.n to ℕ with IsHExp (D.tau i₀) (epsOf D) (conjWt σ lam) h, the condition HOcc (bcAlong (T.tower N g) τ) (j ↦ σ (θ j)) (h i) holds for every i.
premises: hW, the condition HolomorphicLefschetzFormula holds (for Z smooth of relative dimension d and projective over Spec ℂ, finite etale c1 and c2 from Y to Z, F exactly the points y with y followed by c1 equal to y followed by c2, and matrices A y with IsTan and det(1 − A y) ≠ 0, every hodgeH s a b is finite dimensional and the sum over b in range (d+1) of (−1)^b times the trace of hodgeTrace h1 a b composed with hodgePull h2 a b equals the sum over y in F of the X^a coefficient of det(1 + X·A y) divided by det(1 − A y))
second.conclusion: KSAll holds, meaning the six conditions StdEx, KSEx, KSNice, KSGood, KSCong and KSHodge all hold
unclear: Datum (its body is cut, and a second structure of the same name in Tor is also listed)

first_errors: A says that the tower satisfies HOcc "after base change to ℂ", but the Lean text reads "HOcc (bcAlong (T.tower N g) τ) (fun j => σ (θ j)) (h i)" and the dossier shows only "def bcAlong (H : HTower k) {K : Type} [Field K] (τ : k →+* K) : HTower K" without a body, so the meaning of bcAlong is asserted outside the field suggests.
